title: Interfacial Trap and Field Regulation Enables Bias‐Switchable Dual‐Mode Organic Photodetectors for Adaptive Near‐Infrared Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating high‐gain photomultiplication (PM) and low‐power photovoltaic (PV) modes into a single organic photodetector (OPD) enables adaptive sensing across varying light intensities. However, reconciling efficient carrier extraction in the PV mode with high trap‐assisted photomultiplication gain in the PM mode, while maintaining comparable temporal responses, remains challenging. Here, we employ a perovskite nanocrystal@ferroelectric polymer (PNC@FP) composite as a multifunctional interlayer that simultaneously facilitates hole transport and regulates trap‐assisted photomultiplication in dual‐mode OPDs. While the PNCs supply shallow Pb 2+ trap states as the PM‐inducing layer, the FP matrix concurrently partially passivates surface defects to suppress non‐radiative recombination, imposes a permanent dipole field that facilitates hole extraction under 0 V (PV mode), and enhances dielectric screening at the interface, which extends trap‐induced band bending, thereby narrowing the effective barrier for hole tunneling under forward bias. Consequently, the device achieves external quantum efficiency (EQE)/specific detectivity (D*) values of 48.8%/4.18 × 10 12 Jones (PV, 0 V) and 10,656%/3.18 × 10 13 Jones (PM, 1 V) at 850 nm, while maintaining µs‐scale responses in both modes. A programmable circuit further enables autonomous PV/PM switching with light intensity, as demonstrated by real‐time recovery of binary‐coded 850 nm optical signals under dynamically varying illumination.

title: Semiconductor‐Plasmon‐Enabled Efficient Neodymium Electroluminescence in Lead‐Free Perovskite Near‐Infrared Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide‐doped lead‐free perovskite nanocrystals are promising candidates for near‐infrared (NIR) optoelectronics, yet their performance is limited by inefficient exciton‐to‐lanthanide energy‐transfer, surface non‐radiative losses, and intrinsically slow 4f‐4f radiative transitions. Here, we report highly efficient Cs 3 YCl 6 :Sb 3+ , Nd 3+ nanocrystals enabling high‐performance NIR photoluminescence and electroluminescence. The isolated [YCl 6 ] 3− octahedral framework confines excitons and facilitates efficient Sb 3+ ‐induced localized defect‐state emission sensitization to Nd 3+ , leading to intense NIR emissions at 890, 1070, and 1350 nm with an ultra‐high NIR photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 65.9% for Nd 3+ ‐based lead‐free perovskite nanocrystals. Sotalol molecular passivation further suppresses surface non‐radiative recombination and improves energy‐transfer efficiency from 51.5% to 66.8%. Moreover, Cu 2‐x S is introduced as a semiconductor localized surface plasmon resonance layer, its broad NIR plasmonic absorption peak with a maximum near 1070 nm, overlaps well with the Nd 3+ emission, thereby selectively accelerating the spontaneous radiative decay at 890 and 1070 nm by 4.1‐and 9.2‐fold, respectively. Consequently, the optimized NIR light‐emitting diodes delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 10.89%, a peak power density of 3.8 mW cm −2 , and a T 50 lifetime of 389 min, representing a breakthrough among various rare earths‐doped NIR light‐emitting diodes.

title: Gigacycle Fatigue Resistance and Cyclic Phase Separation in Metastable Nanocrystalline Cu–Ag Alloy Thin Films
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanocrystalline metals derive their exceptional strength from a high density of grain boundaries (GBs), but under cyclic loading those same boundaries are unstable, driving abnormal grain growth that seeds fatigue cracking. Solute‐mediated grain boundary stabilization is shown here to extend nanocrystalline fatigue life by orders of magnitude. A metastable nanocrystalline Cu–42 at.% Ag alloy thin film survives 1.2 billion cycles at strain amplitudes exceeding 1.1%. To our knowledge, no other metallic thin film has shown gigacycle fatigue resistance at such extreme strain amplitudes, while comparison with literature data requires care given differences in testing conditions. A combination of microresonator‐based very‐high‐cycle fatigue testing, electron microscopy, and atomistic simulations reveals a composition‐dependent transition in the governing mechanism. In dilute Cu–3Ag, solute clusters kinetically pin interfacial disconnections and slow boundary migration, extending fatigue life but not preventing eventual failure via abnormal grain growth. In contrast, concentrated Cu–42Ag exhibits stable grain boundaries for over a billion cycles. Fatigue damage is ultimately associated with a previously unreported fatigue‐induced phase separation: strain‐enhanced transport decomposes the metastable solid solution into semi‐coherent Cu‐ and Ag‐rich domains. Solute‐stabilized nanocrystalline alloy thin films thus offer a route to gigacycle fatigue resistance in microdevices, and cyclic phase separation emerges as a distinct damage mode.

title: Drug‐Stiffened Polymer Worms: Allostery‐Inspired Activity Gating and Endogenous Enzyme‐Recharged Catalytic Cycling
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural enzymes achieve efficient and specific catalysis through precise allosteric regulation, a dynamic interplay of conformational rigidity and flexibility that remains largely unrealized in synthetic catalysts. Here, we report an allostery‐inspired polymer assembly whose catalytic and therapeutic functions are gated by programmable changes in supramolecular rigidity. The assemblies initially form flexible worm‐like micelles, whereas drug loading induces coordination‐driven crystallization into rigid nanorods. This rigidification restricts substrate accessibility and electron transfer, concurrently suppressing its peroxidase‐like activity, drug cytotoxicity, and fluorescence. In the glutathione (GSH)‐rich tumor microenvironment, disruption of metal coordination reverses rigidification, restores the flexible morphology, and reactivates all functions. The activated assemblies then use tumor‐overexpressed NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) as an endogenous redox partner, channeling reducing equivalents from reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) to replenish their electron reservoir and enable repeated catalytic turnover. This NQO1‐recharged cascade depletes intracellular GSH and NADH while generating cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals, thereby inducing apoptosis, ferroptosis, and cuproptosis, triggering immunogenic cell death, and eliciting robust antitumor immunity in vivo. By integrating allostery‐inspired structure gating with endogenous‐enzyme‐driven catalyst recharging, this work establishes an adaptive catalytic platform that addresses limitations in the activity regulation and redox cycling of artificial enzymes and offers a strategy for catalytic cancer therapy.

title: Machine‐Learning‐Guided Structural Design of Interlayer‐Confined PEI‐Based Composites for Superior Dielectric Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Structural design plays a pivotal role in enhancing the performance of composite materials for electrostatic energy storage, particularly in pulsed power systems operating under extreme conditions. Herein, guided by a sequential multi‐target machine learning (ML) framework, a series of polymer‐based nanocomposites with an interlayer‐confined architecture are fabricated, featuring two‐dimensional in‐plane network formed by interlaced Na 0.5 Bi 0.5 TiO 3 (NBT) nanofibers embedded into the polyetherimide (PEI) matrix. This strategy leverages NBT nanofibers to tailor the spatial electric field distribution via their high dielectric constant, while the fillers simultaneously suppress chain mobility and thereby reduce the matrix diffusivity to reinforce mechanical strength, collectively enhancing breakdown strength and polarization, and thus contributing to excellent electrostatic energy storage capacity. The resulting polymer composite showcases impressive energy storage performance (energy storage density U e = 11.08 J/cm 3 , energy storage efficiency η = 95.46%) and excellent high‐temperature performance ( U e = 5.32 J/cm 3 with η > 90.00%, 150°C), which are far superior to those of most advanced polymer‐based dielectrics reported recently. This work establishes an ML‐guided structural design strategy for next‐generation multilayer polymer dielectrics toward superior energy storage.

title: Ductile Polycrystalline AgCuSe With Preferred Orientation for High Power Density Flexible Thermoelectric Device
abstract: ABSTRACT The recently discovered ductile inorganic thermoelectric (TE) materials provide a promising solution for developing flexible TE devices with high output power density used in wearable electronics. However, the current ductile polycrystalline TE materials are still very rare. In this work, we show that engineering a polycrystal with a strong preferred orientation along the crystal plane with a high ratio of cleavage energy to slip barrier energy can convert it from brittle into ductile. Taking AgCuSe as a case study, via controlling the rolling temperature and speed during the hot‐rolling process, the polycrystalline AgCuSe with (0 k 0) preferred orientation is successfully obtained, which exhibits excellent ductility at room temperature. Likewise, the ductile AgCuSe retains the good TE performance of brittle AgCuSe, with the room‐temperature power factor (∼21.7 µW cm −1 K −2 ) much higher than the best flexible AgCuSe‐based materials reported before. By using the ductile polycrystalline AgCuSe, an ultrathin flexible cross‐plane π‐shaped TE device is developed to show a maximum normalized power density up to 46 µW cm −2 K −2 , a record‐high value in flexible thermoelectrics. This work not only provides a novel ductile TE material for flexible thermoelectrics, but also offers an alternative route to discover more ductile inorganic materials by using the anisotropic mechanical properties.

title: Proton Competition Induced Stabilization in TEMPO‐Based Redox‐Targeting Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT 2,2,6,6‐tetramethylpiperidine‐1‐oxyl (TEMPO) derivatives are widely studied as positive electrolytes in aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) due to their high redox potential. However, TEMPO‐based AORFBs suffer from stability issues with molecule degradation. In this work, a unique stabilization strategy beyond molecular engineering is developed by designing a TEMPO‐based redox‐targeting (RT) flow battery via a proton‐competition mechanism. A RT flow battery is constructed with 4‐acetamido‐TEMPO as redox mediator and polyaniline (PANI) as the solid material, achieving 4.37‐fold enhancement in capacity (35.72 Ah L −1 ), high coulombic efficiency (99.99%) and excellent capacity retention (99.94% per cycle over 500 cycles within 840.82 h). The outstanding stability of the TEMPO‐based flow battery is attributed to the synergistic interaction between proton buffering and RT reactions. This study elucidates a key pathway for suppressing TEMPO radical hydrogenation through a proton competition mechanism, which relies on the reversible doping/de‐doping cycles of the PANI. Operando spectroscopic studies and density functional theory calculations elucidate the mechanism, revealing an intermediate transition state and confirming that proton competition by PANI is pivotal for radical stabilization. This work delves into the mechanism of TEMPO‐based RT flow battery, providing design principles for advancing stable AORFB systems toward long‐duration energy storage applications.

title: Gradient‐Driven Spatial Relay in Titanium Oxynitride for Photocatalytic CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to C 2 H 4 demands simultaneous management of light harvesting, proton supply, and C−C coupling, functions that are difficult to integrate on a single surface site. Here, we present a “surface‐subsurface spatial relay” strategy to overcome this limitation using a gradient titanium oxynitride (G−TiNO) architecture that spatially partitions these steps, realizing CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 conversion without noble metal on Ti‐based catalysts. Operando spectroscopy and DFT reveal that the surface Ti−O layer captures CO 2 and dissociates water to supply *H, while a built‐in electric field drives linear intermediates into a subsurface N−Ti−O domain, where the barrier for *OCCO formation is markedly lowered. Crucially, operando XAFS spectroscopy unveils a reversible “breathing‐mode” adsorption of CO 2 within the gradient architecture, wherein the N−Ti−O lattice dynamically expands and contracts in response to interfacial charge accumulation, stabilizing key intermediates. The optimized G−TiNO−425 achieves a C 2 H 4 evolution rate of 73.34 µmol g −1 h −1 with 76.46% product selectivity and 93.14% electron selectivity. Comparative control experiments show that progressive removal of the TiNO interlayer shifts selectivity from C 2 H 4 to CO, establishing a causal link between the gradient interface and C−C coupling. This work provides a design principle for buried interfaces that exploit dynamic structural flexibility to direct complex multi‐electron photocatalysts.

title: Quinone Carbonyl‐Functionalized Carbon Dots Enable Selective 2e − Oxygen Reduction for Benzyl Alcohol‐Assisted Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) is often limited by competing four‐electron reduction. Here, a precursor‐controlled series of carbon dots (CDs) is developed. The quinone‐associated carbonyl characteristics are systematically tuned by varying the resorcinol‐to‐catechol feed ratio. Across this chemically related series, spectroscopic and electrochemical changes in quinone‐associated surface chemistry correlate with photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production, with resorcinol‐derived CDs ( m ‐CDs) showing the highest activity. In a benzyl alcohol (BA)/ H 2 O biphasic system, BA serves as the reductive substrate, coupling its oxidation with O 2 reduction to H 2 O 2 . A plate‐type microchannel reactor delivers H 2 O 2 production rates of 17.71 and 54.19 mmol g −1 h −1 at 25 and 60°C, respectively, under 450 nm irradiation. In situ spectroscopy and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) show reversible light‐induced changes in carbonyl/oxygen‐containing surface states, and EPR features consistent with semiquinone‐type and ∙ OOH‐related species. Combined with the electrochemical and photocatalytic results, these observations support peroxide‐selective O 2 reduction and motivate a proposed quinone‐associated surface redox model that may involve proton and electron transfer. This work establishes a tunable CDs platform for probing and regulating quinone‐associated surface chemistry in photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production.

title: Breaking the Thermal Limits: Solvation Chemistry of Hydrogel Electrolytes for Extreme‐Temperature Stable Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are promising candidates for safe and cost‐effective energy storage, yet their practical deployment across a wide temperature range is severely constrained by temperature‐dependent ion‐transport limitations and electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability. At low temperatures, sluggish Zn 2+ transport and desolvation promote concentration polarization and nonuniform Zn deposition, while elevated temperatures accelerate water‐induced parasitic reactions, corrosion, and interfacial degradation. Hydrogel electrolytes offer opportunities to address these challenges by regulating water activity, Zn 2+ solvation, ion transport, and interfacial mechanics within an integrated polymer network. This review systematically elucidates five representative design strategies: high‐entropy environments, water‐deficient hydrogels, deep eutectic solvent‐mediated regulation, zwitterionic networks, and nanofiller reinforcement, with particular emphasis on their effects on Zn 2+ coordination, water organization, transport kinetics, and interfacial stability. Quantitative solvation and kinetic descriptors, including coordination numbers, ion‐pair populations, diffusion coefficients, transference numbers, interaction energies, and activation energies, are compared to clarify how electrolyte structure influences performance at different temperatures. The advantages and limitations of the five strategies are further compared in relation to their applicable temperature‐dependent challenges. Finally, key priorities are discussed for temperature‐resolved solvation characterization, operando analysis, practical cell evaluation, and standardized thermal testing, providing guidance for the development of hydrogel electrolytes toward reliable wide‐temperature AZMBs.

title: Light‐Assisted Anion Exchange Membrane Water and Seawater Electrolysis on a Core–Shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing solar energy to assist water and seawater electrolysis represents a promising strategy to reduce the energy input for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its development remains challenging due to limited integration between light‐responsive catalysts and membrane electrolyzer systems. Here, we report a hierarchical core–shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O catalyst that enables efficient light‐assisted hydrogen evolution and is directly interfaced with an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer. The Cu 2 O nanowire core serves as a light‐harvesting scaffold, while the Co‐P nanosheet shell provides active sites, collectively enabling strong light absorption, suppressed reflectivity, and efficient photothermal conversion with localized interfacial heating. The interfacial interaction between Co‐P and Cu 2 O facilitates catalytic kinetics, as supported by experimental analyses, while theoretical calculations reveal optimized charge redistribution and a reduced water dissociation barrier. Under one‐sun irradiation, the catalyst achieves overpotentials of 62 and 253 mV at 10 and 500 mA cm −2 , respectively, in 1 M KOH, with activity enhancement predominantly governed by photothermal effects. When integrated into a light‐assisted AEM electrolyzer, the Co‐P@Cu 2 O||NiFe LDH pair delivers efficient and durable overall water and seawater electrolysis at large current densities. This work establishes a viable strategy for coupling photothermal‐assisted electrocatalysis with membrane electrolyzer systems, advancing solar‐assisted hydrogen production from diverse water resources.

title: Multifunctional Thermo‐Electronic Smart Fabrics Integrating Radiative Cooling and Energy Harvesting for Self‐Powered Intelligent Perception
abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable smart fabrics with integrated thermal regulation and energy autonomy represent a transformative advancement in next‐generation wearable technologies. However, achieving synergistic multifunctionality with a signal platform remains a significant challenge. Herein, we present a multifunctional thermal management and self‐powered smart fabric (TMSPF) that seamlessly integrates passive radiative cooling (PRC) and triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) through a rationally designed functional architecture. The unique all‐fiber structure enables TMSPF good breathability and self‐cleaning properties, thereby providing a dry and comfortable microenvironment for the wearer. Notably, benefiting from the excellent dielectric properties of BaTiO 3 and interconnected porous fiber architecture, the TMSPF achieves excellent PRC capability (a maximum cooling temperature of ∼18.9°C under direct sunlight and a maximum cooling power of 105.9 W m −2 at daytime), as well as enhanced triboelectric output (170 V, 977 mW m −2 ) and high sensitivity (88.72 V kPa −1 ), enabling applications in power supply and intelligent perception. Moreover, TMSPF demonstrates broad application prospects in personal thermal management and raindrop energy harvesting. This synergistic integration effectively addresses the intrinsic trade‐off between energy harvesting and thermal comfort in conventional wearables. This work provides valuable insights into the design and fabrication of next‐generation wearable electronics with integrated thermal and energy functionalities.

title: Fabrication of Tri‐Phase Lithium Alloy in Seconds via an Implosion‐Popcorn Reaction Toward Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Introducing non‐lithium components to fabricate lithium‐based alloy anodes has emerged as a paramount strategy to enhance the processability and stability of lithium metal batteries. However, conventional fabrication suffers from the sluggish wetting kinetics of lithium with non‐lithium components, inducing severe phase heterogeneity and component agglomeration. Herein, we report an ultrafast, spontaneous implosion‐popcorn reaction that explosively disintegrates centimeter‐scale precursor ingots into ultra‐fine particles within seconds, yielding a uniformly dispersed tri‐phase alloy with an interpenetrating network of Fe, Li 3 P, and Li. The as‐obtained lithium alloy exhibits a significantly enhanced Young's modulus and can be processed into different forms, including coatable slurries, self‐standing foils, and active powders. This fabrication method shifts from traditional passive alloying to an active, highly efficient, and homogenous approach. When used as an anode, the homogeneous Li/Fe/Li 3 P architecture facilitates interfacial Li‐ion transfer and regulates initial Li nucleation, thereby promoting dense and uniform Li growth and enabling a cycling lifespan of over 3000 h, together with improved full‐cell stability.

title: Sabatier Principle‐Guided Co‐Solvent Selection for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic co‐solvents can effectively stabilize Zn anodes in rechargeable aqueous batteries, yet their selection remains largely empirical. Here, a Sabatier principle‐analogous framework utilizing molecular polarity index (MPI) as a quantitative descriptor is proposed for rational electrolyte engineering. By investigating a series of C3 alcohol co‐solvents with tunable hydroxyl configurations, we reveal a volcano‐type relationship between MPI and electrochemical performance. Co‐solvents with intermediate MPI, exemplified by 1,3‐propanediol, reside at the apex of this volcano. This optimal polarity strikes a delicate balance between interfacial homogeneity and reaction kinetics, thereby promoting dendrite‐free deposition and suppressing side reactions. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables a symmetric battery to achieve a cumulative plating capacity of 5.2 A h cm −2 and a lifespan exceeding seven months. Furthermore, a high‐mass‐loading (∼30 mg cm −2 ) Zn//I 2 pouch cell (0.3 A h) maintains stable operation over 1200 cycles with a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.057‰ per cycle. More importantly, this framework successfully identifies 1,2,4‐butanetriol as a new highly efficient co‐solvent, demonstrating the robust predictive power of MPI descriptor. This work translates the Sabatier principle into a predictive tool for electrolyte formulation, establishing a generalizable framework for co‐solvent screening that accelerates the development of high‐performance Zn batteries for large‐scale energy storage.

title: Molecular profiling of repeated self-sampled blood reveals dynamic immune phenotypes in young adults
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Although population-based studies of circulating blood proteins have provided profound insight into human biology, transient changes to time-dependent exposures often remain elusive. Here, we perform a longitudinal dried blood spot (DBS) self-sampling study in 808 young adults (aged 24–27, 64% females) from the Swedish Barn [Children], Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm Epidemiology cohort. In total, we collected ~2400 samples from 2020 to 2022. Each sample was profiled for SARS-CoV-2 serological, anti-interferon autoantibodies (AAbs), and 365 inflammation-related proteins. We subsequently linked these samples to registry-confirmed infection and vaccination exposures, physiological traits, genetic variation, and blood counts. We show that data-driven seroclustering captures the response to both infection and vaccination exposures, while stable AAbs against interferon receptors IFNAR1 and IFNGR2 associate with the duration of self-reported COVID-19 symptoms. Genome-wide mapping reveals 664 protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) across 65 proteins, with cis-pQTLs associated proteins showing greater longitudinal stability. Paired pre- and post-exposure samples indicate temporal changes in protein levels after infection (LAP3) and vaccination (TIMP3). This multi-molecular epidemiological profiling of self-sampled blood captures dynamic immune trajectories and shorter-term variability in a population of young adults.

title: Enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of human forebrain development provides insights into autism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cell differentiation is orchestrated by transcription factors binding to enhancers, shaping gene regulatory networks that drive neuronal lineage specification. Deciphering these enhancer-driven networks in human forebrain development is essential for understanding the genetic basis of neurodevelopmental disorders. Through integrative epigenomic and transcriptomic analyses of human forebrain organoids derived from 10 male individuals with autism spectrum disorder and their neurotypical fathers, we construct a comprehensive enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of early neurodevelopment. This network reveals hierarchical regulatory layers upstream of neuronal cell fate genes, experimentally validated via CRISPR interference and loss-of-function analyses. A subnetwork links autism-associated transcriptomic alterations to opposite activities of the transcription factors FOXG1, BHLHE22, EOMES, and NEUROD2, driving increased or decreased excitatory neuron specification in (respectively) macrocephalic or normocephalic individuals with autism. These findings support the association of autism with disruption of enhancer-driven regulatory networks altering neuronal cell fate decisions in the developing fetal brain.

title: Self-adaptive metasurface integrating sensing and active wave control for intelligent wireless communications
abstract: The vision for future wireless networks extends far beyond mere connectivity, fostering spaces that autonomously perceive and adapt to the radio environment. Reconfigurable metasurfaces (RMSs) are designed to tailor wireless propagation through programmable electromagnetic responses. However, conventional RMSs, while assisting communication, lack integrated sensing and self-adaptive control capabilities and suffer from severe path loss along the transmitter-RMS-receiver link. Here we report a self-adaptive metasurface (SA-MS) that integrates sensing and active wave control within a unified platform. Each meta-atom integrates dual-biased PIN diodes and an embedded port, enabling 1-bit programmable reflection and in-band sensing. The sensed waveform is fed to a lightweight convolutional neural network that infers the direction of arrival with robustness against array mismatches. The acquired spatial information is then mapped through a physics-informed surrogate model to an amplitude-phase configuration that works in conjunction with the amplifier to enhance the wireless link. Real-world wireless communication experiments in dynamic environments validate the sensing, decision, and execution loop of SA-MS, with an average signal enhancement of 14.6 dB. This work paves the way for intelligent wireless spaces, where sensing and communication co-evolve at the physical layer.

title: Chemogenetic dissection of the H2O2–salicylic acid feedback loop in PTI and ETI evolutionary conservation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The signaling interplay between hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and salicylic acid (SA) is fundamental to plant stress responses, yet resolving their spatiotemporal dynamics in vivo remains challenging due to spatial ambiguity when using multiple probes. Here, we present RhCy-NI, a single-molecule dual-responsive fluorescent probe featuring orthogonal reaction sites for crosstalk-free detection of H2O2 and SA. The probe exhibits ~25-fold and ~250-fold fluorescence enhancements at 562 and 751 nm, respectively, with detection limits of 96 and 24 nM and high selectivity. Time-course imaging in rice under salt and cadmium stresses reveals that a rapid, transient H2O2 burst precedes SA accumulation. In Nicotiana benthamiana challenged with the Phytophthora infestans elicitin INF1, pharmacological inhibition and SA-deficient genetic backgrounds show that early oxidative signaling is required for SA accumulation, whereas SA sustains a secondary oxidative phase. Genetic analysis reveals that enhanced disease susceptibility 1 (EDS1) primarily supports SA accumulation, whereas helper nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) receptors of the NLR-required-for-cell-death (NRC) family (NRC2/3/4) support both SA accumulation and sustained secondary H2O2 amplification. These findings establish RhCy-NI as a tool for resolving H2O2–SA feedback and implicate components associated with effector-triggered immunity in cell-surface-triggered defense.

title: Theoretical frameworks for credit assignment via behavioral timescale synaptic plasticity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Behavioral Timescale Synaptic Plasticity (BTSP) is a form of plasticity which drives place field formation in hippocampal pyramidal neurons. Unlike traditional learning rules, BTSP learns pre-post correlations on timescales of seconds and rapidly changes single-unit activity in only a few trials. To study how BTSP-like learning can be integrated into network models, we propose a generalized theoretical framework, gBTSP, which we apply to unsupervised and supervised tasks in feedforward and recurrent networks. We show that unsupervised gBTSP learns place field maps in the feedforward case and attractor memories in the recurrent case. For supervised learning, we derive how plateau events can reduce task error, enabling gBTSP to solve trajectory matching and delayed non-match-to-sample tasks. Finally, we find that the speed of credit assignment via gBTSP is limited by network depth or CA3-like recurrence, suggesting that additional mechanisms are necessary to account for BTSP-driven few-shot learning in naturalistic settings.

title: Phenotypic variation in Drosophila complex traits is influenced more by genotype and environmental interactions than by mitonuclear coevolutionary history
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The interdependent relationship between mitochondrial and nuclear genomes is a powerful model for understanding how epistasis shapes the architecture and evolution of complex traits. Once considered a neutral marker, mitochondrial DNA variation is now recognized as critical to phenotypic evolution because of its epistatic interactions and history of coevolution with the nuclear genome. A central challenge in evolutionary genetics is to quantify the relative importance of stabilizing and directional selection shaping complex trait distributions within and among species. Both can act on interacting and/or co-evolving genes contributing to quantitative traits, but resolving their relative roles is complicated by the complex architecture of most traits. Here, we use a panel of 90 Drosophila mitonuclear genotypes to quantify the relative contributions of mitochondrial, nuclear, and environmental variation and their interactions to four metabolically demanding complex traits. We sample both within-species and between-species mitochondrial variation and observe stronger interaction effects attributable to within-species variation, consistent with stabilizing selection maintaining mitonuclear function. Additionally, culturing the flies on a mitochondrial Complex I inhibitor, rotenone, reveals significant genotype × environment (G × E and G × G × E) interaction effects, providing insight into how genetic variation can be maintained across changing environments.

title: DPI-score: a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived assemblies
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Advances in cryoEM have led to a surge in high-resolution structures; however, model building and refinement at resolutions ( > = 3 Å) and in regions with variable local resolution remain challenging, making validation essential. CryoEM derived assemblies often contain extensive protein-protein interfaces, however, most existing validation metrics focus on density fit or overall geometry without directly assessing interface quality. To address this, we present DPI-Score, a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived complexes. The method uses only raw structural coordinates of interface atoms, without requiring engineered features, and achieves 87.53% validation accuracy. DPI-Score was applied to 29,120 interfaces from 6,011 fitted entries with resolutions worse than 3 Å in the Electron Microscopy Data Bank. Here, we show that DPI-Score provides complementary information to existing validation metrics and can identify interface errors in modelled assemblies that are not detected by density-based scores alone.
