title: Glutamine binding and sodium coordination reveal the transport mechanism of y⁺LAT1/CD98hc
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The heteromeric amino acid transporter y⁺LAT1/CD98hc (SLC7A7/SLC3A2) mediates electroneutral exchange of cationic and neutral amino acids, with Na⁺ required for efficient transport of neutral substrates. Loss-of-function mutations cause Lysinuric Protein Intolerance (LPI), and emerging evidence highlights the physiological relevance of L-glutamine uptake in immune and bone cells. Here, we present the cryo-EM structure of human y⁺LAT1/CD98hc at 3.4 Å resolution in an outward-open conformation bound to L-glutamine, revealing a non-canonical substrate-binding pose involving Cys320 in TM8. Combining docking and molecular dynamics simulations, and functional assays, we identify a Na+-binding tetrad (Asn49–Ser131–Gly323–Ser327) that underlies Na⁺-dependent transport of neutral amino acids. By contrast, cationic substrates such as L-arginine occupy the same locus with their positively charged side chain, effectively replacing the role of Na⁺ and enabling Na⁺-independent exchange. Mutagenesis and kinetic analyses support this mechanism and reveal a key role for Glu128 during transitions toward inward-facing conformations, providing structural insight into the transport cycle. Collectively, these findings establish how y⁺LAT1 integrates Na⁺ and substrate recognition to mediate the selective exchange of neutral and cationic amino acids.

title: A split RNA-guided Cas9 system for PAM-independent and cis-cleavage-free nucleic acid detection
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The CRISPR-Cas9 system exhibits limited trans-cleavage activity, restricting its utility for nucleic acid detection. Here, we present a split RNA-guided Cas9 system (SCas9) that overcomes this limitation. By partitioning single-guide RNA into functionally independent scaffold and spacer modules, SCas9 enables amplification-free detection of single-stranded DNA and RNA with picomolar sensitivity within 30 min and single-nucleotide specificity. Incorporation of λ exonuclease permits PAM-independent detection of double-stranded DNA without cis-cleavage activity. Coupling SCas9 with recombinase polymerase amplification or reverse transcription–recombinase polymerase amplification extends detection of double-stranded DNA and long RNA to attomolar sensitivity. We further developed an autocatalytic SCas9 strategy for attomolar microRNA detection. SCas9 demonstrates broad substrate compatibility and was validated in clinical specimens, including human papillomavirus 16 in vaginal secretions and miR-21 in colorectal cancer tissues, highlighting its potential for point-of-care diagnostics.

title: Single cell RNA sequencing reveals unexpected heterogeneity and identifies AP2XI-6 as a mature bradyzoite specific cell cycle regulator
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Toxoplasma gondii prevalence is due, in part, to its ability to persist in hosts while retaining the capacity to transmit and recrudesce. This process, while critical, is poorly understood. Through single cell RNA profiling of in vivo-derived bradyzoites, we show that bradyzoites are heterogeneous and not G1-arrested, as expected from in vitro studies. Instead, they progress through two distinct cell cycles that branch from a single G1 state. One is common amongst tachyzoites and in vitro- and in vivo-derived bradyzoites; the other is newly identified within the population of in vivo-derived bradyzoites. While in G1b, these in vivo-derived bradyzoites express cyst wall proteins predicted to replenish the wall that protects cysts and prevents clearance. We demonstrate that AP2XI-6, a putative AP2-transcription factor expressed by bradyzoites in G1 in vivo, is dispensable for tachyzoite growth and cyst formation in vitro but necessary for encystation or persistence in vivo. We propose that AP2XI-6 is a driver of replication through the newly identified in vivo bradyzoite specific cell cycle and that this is required for cyst maturation or persistence.

title: Sensory cortical disinhibition underlies long-term fear memory in humans
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: How transient threats turn into persistent, long-term fear memories is a fundamental problem in neuroscience, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Early sensory cortex, traditionally viewed as a passive feature analyzer, is increasingly recognized as an active participant in fear processing. Combining high-definition α-frequency transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD α-tACS) with simultaneous EEG-fMRI (electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging) and transformer-based neural decoding, we tracked fear memory development across formation, consolidation, and long-term retention (assessed at 15 min, 24 h, and 7 days after fear conditioning). Spatiotemporal memory traces were identified at all three assessments, beginning at an early sensory stage (40–60 ms post-stimulus) and distributed across visual cortex and limbic regions. Conditioning potentiated occipital α-oscillation desynchronization, a marker of visual cortical disinhibition, which subsequently predicted the strength of long-term memory traces. Critically, targeted α-tACS over early visual cortex induced early visual cortical (V1/V2) inhibition, abolished conditioning-potentiated α desynchronization, and selectively disrupted fear-memory consolidation and retention while leaving initial acquisition intact. These findings establish sensory cortical disinhibition as a necessary mechanism for long-term fear memory in humans and identify early sensory cortex as crucial node for intervention of persistent maladaptive fear.

title: Functional diversity of GPCR–Gustducin complexes controls signaling output and suppresses alternative pathways
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gustducin (Ggust), the G protein mediating taste receptor signaling, is expressed not only in sensory taste cells but throughout the human body alongside numerous non-taste G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Whether and how these receptors engage Ggust, and the functional consequences of such interactions, remain poorly understood. Here, we develop two complementary biosensors that enable direct monitoring of GPCR–Ggust interaction and downstream signaling in living cells, allowing pharmacological characterization of Ggust activity induced by non-taste GPCRs. We find that several non-taste GPCRs do not activate Ggust but instead stabilize the G protein heterotrimer and suppress basal signaling by forming unproductive GPCR–G protein complexes, whereas others induce conventional Ggust activation and signal transduction. We further show that these unproductive GPCR–Ggust complexes suppress the activation of alternative signaling pathways by sequestering receptors from other G proteins. This mode of interaction functionally partitions GPCRs into activators and inactivators of Ggust and represents a mechanism for balancing concurrent signaling pathways within a cell.

title: Spiro-OMeTAD-Inspired Molecular Design: Electron Tunneling Meets Halogen Bonding for Robust Buried Interfaces
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs) are limited by fragile buried interfaces and uncontrolled nucleation. These get exacerbated when conventional hole-transport materials such as spiro-OMeTAD are used with dopants, especially in inverted p–i–n devices, leading to accelerated ion migration and poor stability. To overcome these limitations, we introduce BDTP-4D, a spiro-OMeTAD-inspired bis-dithienopyrrole molecule designed to mimic its merits while avoiding dopant-induced instability. Applied as a self-assembled monolayer (SAM) atop NiOx, BDTP-4D was co-sensitized with triphenylamine derivatives possessing targeted functionalities (–Br, –SMe, –OMe), which modulated hole-transport-layer surface energy and directed perovskite nucleation and crystallization. This yielded pinhole-free films with large, homogeneous grains atop the co-sensitized electrodes. Mechanistic analysis revealed complementary buried-interfacial processes: NiOx–Br electronic coupling and halogen-bonding between Br and Sn perovskite (BDTP:Br), and sulfur-mediated passivation (BDTP:SMe). This mixed-SAM strategy reproduces the benefits of doped spiro-OMeTAD while eliminating interfacial instability, thereby defining a generalizable molecular design principle for robust buried interfaces across emerging photovoltaics.

title: Multi-ancestry genetic analysis reveals 29 novel rheumatoid arthritis loci, effector genes and drug repurposing opportunities
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a complex autoimmune disease with a substantial heritable component. We perform multi-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analyses of 351,498 individuals (comprising 39,600 RA cases and 311,898 controls) by integrating published and new datasets. This analysis identifies 29 novel RA susceptibility loci and systematically classifies association signals as population-specific, population-dominant, or population-shared between East Asian and European populations. Bayesian fine-mapping and functional annotation prioritize putative causal variants, highlighting 67 variants with posterior inclusion probability>0.1 in novel loci, including an SLC27A6 missense variant (rs137898880) and a STIM1 3′ UTR variant (rs3750996). Our gene-prioritization framework combining genetic and biological evidence identifies 203 high-confidence effector genes, 16 of which reside in novel loci (e.g., IFI16, AIM2, RGS1, ITPKB, CD80, RHOH, NFKB1, SIK3, and CCND2). Colocalization analysis leveraging tissue-specific eQTL datasets provides mechanistic insights by implicating shared causal variants underlying RA association signals. Notably, the transcription factor gene RUNX3 at a novel locus shows evidence of cis-regulation in immune cells, and RUNX3-binding sites are enriched for variants explaining excess RA heritability, suggesting a potential role for RUNX3 as a trans-regulatory mediator of RA risk at distal RA loci. Finally, exploratory gene-drug interaction networks weighted by RA association strength highlight population-informed therapeutic opportunities and drug-repurposing targets driven largely by novel loci.

title: Built-in electric field driven MXene/perovskite Schottky heterojunction for photo-electro-thermal energy redistribution in thermochromic smart windows
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Perovskite-based thermochromic smart windows offer a sustainable solution for energy-efficient building technologies. However, existing strategies to reconcile the transition temperature of thermochromic perovskites with practical application temperatures primarily rely on extrinsic composite engineering, often neglecting the intrinsic multi-energy field conversion and photo-electro-thermal coupling effects of perovskites. Here, we introduce a band structure engineering strategy by constructing a MXene/perovskite Schottky heterojunction, leveraging an interfacial built-in electric field to induce photon energy redistribution. The Fermi level alignment between Ti3C2Tx and MAPbI3-xClx facilitates light-activated band bending, which enhances ultraviolet/visible photon harvesting for charge generation (photoelectric channel), complementing the inherent broadband photothermal effect of MXene (photothermal channel). This dual-energy utilization pathway, integrated within a MXene-enhanced perovskite architecture, significantly enhances the photo-electro-thermal performance. The fabricated multilayer Cl-doped perovskite smart window demonstrates a self-induced room-temperature thermochromic transition with a narrow thermal hysteresis of 5.2 °C and a 55% enhancement in photocurrent density. It also exhibits scalable manufacturability, competitive stability, extensive energy-saving performance, and multi-band communication compatibility. This work establishes a universal design paradigm for thermally responsive materials, and the multi-channel photon energy utilization strategy can be extended to other energy-efficient phase-transition systems, with promising implications for global carbon neutrality efforts.

title: Global patterns of radial growth-structural heterogeneity relationships in forests
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Classical theory predicts that environmental improvement intensifies competition and increases forest structural heterogeneity (variation in tree radial size). Whether warmer and wetter conditions drive convergence in stress-dominated regions remains unknown. Using a global tree-ring dataset ( > 900 sites, > 55,000 cores) with mixed-effects and mediation models, and accounting for Taylor’s law, we show that the negative growth–structure correlation is widespread, but its absolute slope increases along the stress gradient and becomes non-significant in low-stress regions (warm low-altitude, South Temperate, and tropics). Climate-to-structure pathways shift from growth-mediated in stress-dominated regions to non-significant in low-stress regions, with mediation strength increasing from temperate to alpine zones. On the Tibetan Plateau, warmer and wetter conditions are associated with homogenization via enhanced radial growth and reduced climate sensitivity. These findings challenge the classical expectation that environmental improvement inevitably increases structural heterogeneity, revealing a shift from stress-driven convergence to decoupling under low stress and providing a unified framework for predicting forest responses to climate change.

title: Boosting reinforcement learning for critical node detection with multi-topology training strategies
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Identifying pivotal components in complex networks—such as key intersections in transportation systems, influential actors in social networks, or keystone species in ecosystems—is essential for improving the resilience and mitigating catastrophic failures of these systems. However, existing methods for critical node detection are typically tailored to specific network types and objectives, limiting their generalizability. To overcome this limitation, we propose a machine learning framework that combines reinforcement learning with an attention-based graph neural network. By leveraging multi-topology training, our model learns to adapt and generalize across diverse network structures and objective functions. Experiments on real-world and synthetic networks uncover distinct topological features that are important for identifying critical nodes. Notably, our method applied to personalized gene networks, prioritizes genes that are significantly enriched for cataloged cancer drivers. This work provides a robust critical node detection model with a comprehensive multi-topology training approach, suitable for a broader range of real-world applications.

title: Chirality-locked low-dimensional bound states in the continuum lasers
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) support high-quality-factor resonances embedded in extended spectra, and their radiation properties can be tailored through perturbative symmetry breaking and chiral engineering. However, because BICs are intrinsically delocalized states of infinite periodic structures, they typically require large spatial footprints. Achieving localized BIC modes while preserving radiation suppression and topological singularities, and simultaneously enabling chiral responses, remains a challenge. Here, we experimentally realize low-threshold BIC lasers localized at one-dimensional interfaces and zero-dimensional junctions by interfacing domains with identical bulk BIC characteristics but opposite chirality. The resulting interfaces and junctions host spatially localized states that exhibit optical spin–momentum-locked emission governed by the assigned chirality, while retaining intrinsic BIC properties, including narrow far-field divergence and pump-selective lasing localization. In addition, polarization singularities confirm the topological nature of these low-dimensional BICs, particularly the well-defined topological charge of the zero-dimensional junction mode. Coupling two zero-dimensional BICs further gives rise to bonding and antibonding supermodes, enabling non-Hermitian, chirality-locked behaviors. These results establish a route to compact, high-quality-factor photonic states with engineered chirality through dimensional reduction of BICs, without relying on defect confinement or band inversion.

title: An electrically driven multimodal soft robot enabled by a monolithic heterolayer elastomer
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Soft robots powered by active materials can navigate complex environments through multimodal locomotion. However, prevailing designs typically rely on a single active material within multi-component architectures, which often leads to high structural complexity and “soft-stiff” interfacial challenges. Here, we present an electrically driven, entirely soft robot based on a monolithic heterolayer elastomer integrating a processable high-performance dielectric elastomer and a liquid crystal elastomer. In this “soft-soft” structure, the liquid crystal elastomer functions as a reconfigurable compliant skeleton to program the equilibrium states, while the dielectric elastomer serves as a fast-responsive artificial muscle driving dynamic motion. Through independent control of the two active materials, the robot demonstrates bidirectional crawling at 2.3 cm·s−1, leaping over 2.5 body lengths, climbing on a 20° slope, and controlled rolling. Our approach establishes a paradigm for creating soft robots with high structural integrity, payload‑to‑weight ratio, and controllability for deployment in unstructured environments.

title: Tuning methanol-CO selectivity in CO2 hydrogenation by Ga coordination engineering in ZnGa2O4
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Structure sensitivity limits the rational control of CO2 hydrogenation over oxide catalysts, yet how cation coordination governs product selectivity in spinel remains unclear. A synthesis-structure-mechanism framework for ZnGa2O4 is established by linking Ga coordination to methanol and CO production. Ammonia-mediated coprecipitation favors octahedrally coordinated Ga, whereas organic-assisted hydrothermal synthesis enriches tetrahedrally coordinated Ga. Catalytic measurements, structural characterization, in-situ spectroscopy and calculations show that Ga coordination is associated with reaction pathway selection, while surface area, crystallinity and oxygen vacancies also influence CO2 conversion. Octahedral Ga-rich surfaces readily form oxygen vacancies and expose Zn-containing sites, promoting the hydrogenation of formate intermediates to methanol. In contrast, tetrahedral Ga-rich surfaces suppress extensive vacancy formation and favor a carboxyl-mediated pathway to CO. This coordination-based framework links synthesis to operando active-site structure and product distribution, providing a general strategy for programming methanol/CO product distributions in Zn-based spinel catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation.

title: Kinetic balancing for near-equilibrium growth of defect-suppressed lead bromide perovskite single crystals
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Controlling crystallization pathways for solution-grown lead-bromide perovskites remains a major unresolved challenge. Herein, we present a ligand-regulated crystallization strategy that achieves near-equilibrium growth for lead-bromide perovskite single crystals. Such regulation mitigates kinetic imbalance during crystal growth, thereby suppressing non-equilibrium defect incorporation, improving lattice coherence, and facilitating spatially uniform crystal growth. This strategy is applicable to a representative set of lead-bromide perovskites. Specifically, the resulting CsPbBr3 single crystals exhibit a high resistivity of 5.1 × 1010 Ω·cm and carrier mobility up to 93.95 cm2·V−1·s−1. Reduced electron-phonon coupling weakens optical-phonon scattering and raises the effective thermally activated conduction barrier from 0.43 to 0.71 eV, extending stable bias operation from 40 to 200 V·mm−1. These advances enable sensitive and stable ionizing-radiation detection under both photon-counting and charge-integrating modes. Overall, this work establishes a general kinetic-design principle for defect-suppressed, near-equilibrium crystallization of lead-bromide perovskites, enabling reliable high-field operation for ionizing-radiation detectors.

title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe2: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: One of the recurring hurdles in studying unconventional superconductivity is the challenge of efficiently and conclusively identifying the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in a new material. Uranium ditelluride (UTe2) exhibits an unprecedented number of superconducting phases, and none of them has had its symmetry conclusively identified so far. Here we report results of an extensive study of the thermal conductivity of UTe2 in the superconducting state as a function of the angle of an applied magnetic field rotated in the b-c plane. We observe substantial oscillations in the thermal conductivity as a function of field angle, and, utilizing the experimentally determined Fermi surface, we model this phenomenon for all potential gap structures in UTe2. This allows us to identify point nodes near the b-axis, implying that the superconducting order parameter most likely belongs to the B2u irreducible representation of the crystal point group.

title: Agricultural economic responses to ecoclimate teleconnections induced by forest loss
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Forest disturbances are increasing globally, altering vegetation in ways that can affect distant agricultural systems through ecoclimate teleconnections. We examine how large-scale U.S. regional forest loss with C3 grass replacement affects agricultural production and markets. We integrate climate simulations, econometric yield models, and an agricultural sector model to trace impacts from vegetation change through climate anomalies to yields, land allocation, prices, and welfare, while isolating vegetation-driven effects from greenhouse-gas forcing. Teleconnection-induced yield responses are spatially heterogeneous. Soybean yields decline, particularly in the Southern Plains, while wheat gains occur there and corn responses are muted. This shifts regional crop mixes and increases total production by 1–3%, lowering crop prices, increasing consumer surplus, and reducing producer surplus, with small positive net agricultural welfare effects. Our study excludes forest-sector impacts and ecosystem-service losses and therefore does not imply that forest loss is beneficial.

title: Emergent mesoscale nanoparticle patterns from a non-equilibrium liquid lens
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Colloidal nanoparticles can assemble into richly structured materials, yet the complex morphologies that emerge under non-equilibrium conditions are often viewed as irreproducible artifacts. Here we show that evaporating a lens-shaped colloidal suspension at a fluid–fluid interface produces a robust cascade of nanoparticle film morphologies, ranging from continuous monolayers to perforated films, ribbon networks, and isolated tiles. Using in situ confocal microscopy and ex situ electron microscopy together with coupled cross-scale simulations, we identify the physical principles that govern this sequence. A macroscopic transport model determines the deposition history imposed by evaporation, which drives a nanoscale kinetic Monte Carlo model capturing particle rearrangement and solvent-mediated kinetic arrest. A coarse-grained Cahn–Hilliard–Stokes framework rationalizes the observed mesoscale periodicity as a finite-wavelength instability of the evolving film. By tuning concentration and solvent volatility, we control the system’s trajectory through this dynamic phase space and establish a predictable framework for navigating non-equilibrium nanoparticle assembly.

title: A Miniaturized Electrostatic Field Sensor Based on MOS Depletion-Layer Capacitance Modulation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Static and low-frequency electric fields are ubiquitous in natural and engineered systems. Space-charge accumulation, migration, and dissipation regulate local field distributions and are central to dielectric characterization, high-voltage insulation assessment, and power electronic device analysis. However, existing measurement approaches remain limited for embedded online electrostatic field monitoring by mechanical structures, grounding requirements, system size, and complex external readout. Here, we report a miniaturized electrostatic field sensor based on MOS depletion-layer capacitance modulation. An external electric field is converted by an induction electrode into an equivalent bias voltage, which modulates the depletion-layer width and total capacitance of a MOS structure and is read out by a bias-tunable MOS capacitance bridge. By engineering the MOS C–V operating window, the depletion response is positioned within a monotonic regime suitable for bipolar electric field measurements. After calibration in a parallel-plate electrode system, the sensor achieves a measurement range of ±1000 kV/m, a resolution of 178 V/m, and a linearity of 0.9999. Monitoring surface-charge evolution on insulating materials and scanning of surface electric fields on power devices demonstrate that this MOS-based sensor enables miniaturized, floating, and low-perturbation electrostatic field measurements at charged interfaces and in device environments.

title: Light-driven oxidative coupling of methane via charge-symmetry-breaking
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Light-driven oxidative coupling of methane into C2+ chemicals represents a sustainable route towards carbon-neutral management, yet faces critical challenges including narrow solar spectrum utilization, inefficient charge carrier dynamics, and tricky C − C coupling. Herein, we achieve highly active and selective light-driven methane conversion to C2+ chemicals over multi-interfacial CuO/ZnO heterojunction. Mechanistic investigations reveal that charge redistribution at CuO/ZnO interface creates interfacial sites with unbalanced electronic states, which promote methane dissociation, alleviate coupling energy of methyl intermediates, and suppress electrostatic repulsion, thereby facilitating C − C coupling. Additionally, Z-Scheme charge transfer spatially decouples oxygen reduction on CuO and methane oxidation on ZnO, respectively. Consequently, CuO/ZnO delivers an ethane yield of 30.87 mmol g−1 h−1 with a C2+ selectivity up to 97.8%, an apparent quantum yield of 3.9% at 420 nm and a durability of 124 h. Here, we show that charge symmetry breaking provides a feasible strategy for converting methane to high-value C2+ chemicals.

title: Photocatalytic radical hydrogenation of unactivated alkenes via an intermolecular hydrogen-atom-transfer relay
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the ubiquity of alkene reduction in chemical synthesis, developing safe, general, and chemoselective hydrogenation methods that avoid pressurized hydrogen gas or precious metals remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a redox-neutral photocatalytic radical transfer hydrogenation strategy that addresses these constraints via an intermolecular hydrogen-atom-transfer (HAT) relay. This approach leverages a synergistic diaryl ketone–cobalt–thiol triple catalytic system to utilize naturally abundant γ-terpinene as a sustainable hydrogen donor. Driven by visible light, the reaction proceeds through a HAT cascade to generate a reactive cobalt–hydride species, enabling the efficient hydrogenation of a broad spectrum of unactivated alkenes—ranging from terminal to sterically demanding tetrasubstituted variants—under mild, additive-free conditions. The protocol exhibits excellent chemoselectivity, preserving sensitive functionalities such as aldehydes, epoxides, carboxylic acids, and Lewis basic heterocycles. The practical utility of this protocol is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis with low catalyst loadings, establishing a versatile and environmentally benign platform for alkene reduction.

title: Taming crystallization to achieve superior soft magnetic performance via fine nanocrystallines
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The increasing demand for high-efficiency power electronics in emerging technologies such as 5 G and artificial intelligence is limited by the intrinsic trade-off between high saturation magnetic flux density (Bs) and low coercivity (Hc) in soft magnetic materials. Here, we report a rotational magnetic field annealing strategy for Fe-(Co)-Si-B-Cu-Nb and Fe-Co-B-P alloys that enables precise control of crystallization kinetics. The applied rotational magnetic field promotes dynamic structural fluctuations in amorphous precursors, enhancing nucleation while suppressing grain growth. Consequently, fine nanocrystalline structures with grain sizes of 1–5 nm are obtained, achieving a high Bs of 1.94 T and a low Hc of ~0.8 A m−1. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that rotational magnetic fields generate spatially heterogeneous fluctuations, facilitating dense and uniform nucleation. This work provides a pathway for designing fine nanocomposite soft magnetic materials through external-field-controlled crystallization.

title: A subspecialty diagnostic system powered by self-supervised learning for cervical histopathology
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major malignancy in women, with large-scale human papillomavirus-based screening generating a large volume of biopsies and, for advanced cases, surgical specimens, imposing an overwhelming diagnostic burden that necessitates precise histopathological evaluation. Although deep learning shows promise, general foundation models offer a broader reach but remain limited in capturing subspecialty-specific features and task adaptability. We introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, built upon the subspecialized dataset and developed through two synergistic pretraining stages: self-supervised learning on approximately 190 million tissue patches to build a cervical-specific feature extractor, and multimodal enhancement with 2.5 million image-text pairs, followed by diagnostic functions integration and downstream task enhancement. CerS-Path integrates eight functions—across morphological diagnosis, predictive analytics, and multimodal tasks—to cover the diagnostic workflow from biopsies to resection specimens. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate improved performance in cervical pathology in female patients, where CerS-Path outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across 26 of 30 diagnostic tasks. Furthermore, in multicenter retrospective and prospective validation across six independent cohorts of women, CerS-Path achieves up to 99% sensitivity for clinically relevant lesion detection with acceptable specificity across sites, highlighting its potential for screening-derived histopathology and suitability for integration into high-volume diagnostic pathways.

title: Geophysical conditions favoring precursory slip before major earthquakes
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Precursory slow slip holds potential for reliable earthquake forewarning, yet the conditions conducive to it remain elusive. While quite a number of large earthquakes on smooth megathrust faults are preceded by precursory slow slip, laboratory experiments suggest such slip is inhibited on smooth faults. Here we capture diverse preseismic slow slip behaviors through laboratory experiments, and show that the occurrence pattern of precursory slow slip is dictated by both fault roughness and stress. We find that energetic slow slip producing pronounced acceleration in preseismic moment release prevails on smooth faults under low stress but diminishes as stress increases. For rougher faults, multiple slow slips yield moderate to pronounced acceleration depending on stress. Our results extend previous observations by showing that under lower normal stress, precursor signals on smooth faults can be more pronounced than those on rougher faults, reconciling the contradiction between field and laboratory observations. Our findings provide a mechanism for the prevalence of precursory phase for large earthquakes on smooth, fluid-rich megathrust faults.

title: Bright and stable near-infrared tin-perovskite LEDs enabled by efficient optical and thermal management
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Invisible near-infrared (NIR) light sources are central to optoelectronic and bioelectronic systems including night-vision imaging, facial recognition, and non-invasive biomedical sensing. However, realizing planar NIR emitters with high output optical power remains a major challenge. Here we demonstrate lead-free CsSnI3 perovskite light-emitting diodes (LEDs) that achieve simultaneous breakthroughs in efficiency, radiance and operational stability. The devices deliver high radiances of 6304 W sr−1 m−2 under DC and 21,633 W sr−1 m−2 under pulsed driving, together with a half-lifetime (T50) of 64.3 h at 100 mA cm−2, representing record performance for NIR tin-based perovskite LEDs and a substantial advance for solution-processed NIR optoelectronics. These advances are enabled by the spontaneous formation of discrete hemispherical perovskite microstructures, which synergistically enhance optical and thermal management. We further demonstrate the effectiveness of large-area planar LEDs for red-glow-free night-vision surveillance, biomedical imaging and sensing. Our work establishes a viable route toward high-radiance, stable and lead-free NIR light sources, advancing the development of scalable perovskite-based optoelectronic and bioelectronic technologies.

title: Sunflower pollen microgels enable sonication-free dispersion of carbon nanotubes for bio-based conductive inks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sustainable, high-performance conductive inks are crucial for wearable electronics. While biopolymer-based dispersants offer renewable and biocompatible routes for CNT inks, a paradox persists: biopolymers require energy-intensive extraction, high-power ultrasonication, and lack the rheological strength for precision extrusion printing. Here we show that a sonication-free strategy utilizing sunflower pollen microgels in their native granular state, leveraging their amphiphilic spiky architecture, achieves CNT debundling through a mild-stirring-driven capture-collision-friction integrated process, while alginate provides electrostatic stabilization. The resulting pollen-alginate-CNT (PAC) inks exhibit rapid thixotropy and high viscoelasticity, enabling high-fidelity 3D extrusion and screen printing. Drying induces a lamella-like assembly, forming anisotropic conductive networks. These features unlock multifunctional performance, including humidity sensing via interlayer-spacing modulation, direction-dependent strain sensing, and electromagnetic interference shielding. This work establishes a scalable, energy-efficient framework that overcomes the processing and rheological limitations of conventional bio-based inks, advancing sustainable, adaptive printed electronic systems.

title: Energy poverty in an era of geopolitical instability: The role of Chinese FDI and south–south cooperation in Africa
abstract: The rising geopolitical fragmentation, driven by geopolitical tensions, conflicts and wars, has reshaped the global energy landscape, increasing uncertainty and vulnerability in energy markets. These disruptions present serious challenges for different economies in the Global South, where countries already face significant difficulties in facilitating energy transition and mitigating energy poverty. In this context, South-South cooperation may represent an important tool to address energy challenges, particularly through foreign investment. This study investigates the contribution of Chinese FDI to reducing energy poverty in Africa through different channels and whether conflict conditions influence the extent to which Chinese FDI contributes to improving energy outcomes. Our study contributes to the literature on the role of Chinese foreign capital in reducing energy poverty in Africa by examining both the underlying mechanisms and the potential role of conflict conditions in shaping these effects. To empirically explore this complex nexus, we rely on Structural Equation Modelling using a set of energy and socioeconomic variables from 2005 to 2022. The findings reveal a significant positive association between Chinese FDI and energy performance, with the prosperity channel representing the main mechanism. This association appears weaker in conflict-affected contexts, suggesting that geopolitical stability conditions the extent to which foreign investment is associated with improved energy outcomes. Policymakers in the region should consider creating a more attractive and stable investment environment to promote trade ties with Chinese companies, as these ties could be used as a tool to alleviate energy poverty.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: The Iberian blackout: A black swan or a gray rhino? A protection-aware dynamic voltage security assessment
abstract: On 28 April 2025, the Iberian power system collapsed after a rapid voltage rise that led to widespread generation disconnections and loss of synchronism. The final report of the ENTSO-E Expert Panel attributes the blackout to several interacting factors including ineffective voltage control, fixed power factor operation, misaligned protection settings, manual shunt reactor switching, and limited observability. These factors raise a general question: given the current state, can the next trip, ramp, topology action, or shunt switching raise the voltages measured by overvoltage relays above their settings before voltage controls respond? We answer it with a protection-aware dynamic voltage security assessment. For each candidate event, the method computes the voltage at every overvoltage relay over the relay time window from a dynamic model of the network, its controls, and its relays. It predicts which relays trip after a first trip, identifies assets whose relay or measurement data are insufficient for a safety conclusion, and, when one exists, computes a minimum-cost fast reactive power action that keeps all relay voltages below their settings. Case studies on four benchmark systems and a 2000-bus system that reproduces the mechanism of the Iberian blackout show that the method flagged every event that caused a secondary trip within the relay window, never declared safe a plant that tripped within that window, and, on the benchmarks, found fast reactive power actions that prevented the trips within the relay window whenever it judged such actions feasible. These results were validated with nonlinear time-domain simulations. The code is publicly available.

title: Decoupling instantaneous and cumulative stress: Physics-guided capacity prediction for lithium-ion batteries under stochastic cycling
Urban pollution island and urban heat island jointly worsen solar PV power potential in China
Comparative assessment of angular-selective radiative cooling performance for urban buildings under future climate scenarios
Common-path evaluation of electric boiler and thermal storage dispatch in Finnish district heating under electricity-price uncertainty
abstract: The value of uncertainty-aware district-heating dispatch depends on when prices become known and how long heat remains in storage. This study develops a price-taking mixed-integer linear model for a Finnish system with biomass CHP, a 50 MW th electric boiler (EB), a natural-gas peak boiler, and thermal energy storage (TES). Daily 72 h problems implement the cleared first 24 h and propagate each policy's realised TES state. Deterministic, stochastic, and budgeted robust policies are compared on one 2023 hourly path and on 800 held-out price trajectories; their economic differences are assessed against TES value and parameter sensitivity. With 200 MWh th TES, annual costs are EUR 4.902, 4.920, and 4.939 million, respectively, compared with EUR 4.783 million for a rolling perfect-foresight benchmark. Stochastic dispatch has the lowest held-out mean cost and regret, while deterministic dispatch has slightly lower P 95 and CVaR 95 . TES saves EUR 1.974 million a − 1 relative to matched no-storage dispatch; the stochastic and robust annual premiums are only EUR 0.037 and 0.075/MWh th . Storage mainly shifts heat within one day. A 200-sample annual rolling sensitivity analysis identifies CHP power-to-heat ratio, EB capacity, fuel price, and TES duration as the dominant cost drivers. Biases of ±5% and ± 10% in look-ahead heat demand preserve the annual policy ranking. The EB dispatch-weighted carbon intensity is approximately 26 g CO2/kWhel, below the national consumption-weighted mean of 37.69 g CO2/kWhel.

title: Photovoltaic greenhouses in the European south: balancing energy generation and agricultural productivity - an economic analysis
abstract: This study evaluates the techno-economic feasibility of photovoltaic greenhouses in representative Mediterranean regions in Spain and Italy. A techno-economic model was developed to analyze the interaction between photovoltaic technology choice including present-day crystalline silicon PV (c-Si), current-state Organic Photovoltaics (OPV) modules with 63 W m −2 , and a projected future OPV scenario with 145 W m −2 , greenhouse electricity demand profiles, PV coverage levels, battery storage integration, remuneration schemes and crop yield responses to shading. Without taking crop yields into account, results show that greenhouse electricity demand and the resulting self-consumption potential are the dominant drivers of economic performance. Under high-demand conditions several configurations become profitable, reaching net present values (NPVs) of up to 51,640€ in Bari and 22,176€ in Almería. Under the optimistic OPV145 scenario, which combines a projected module output of 145 W m −2 with future upscaling-related cost reductions, NPVs reach values comparable to the present-day c-Si PV reference in selected high-demand configurations. Profitability declines under less favorable performance assumptions, with initial performance losses exerting a stronger economic effect than higher annual degradation rates. The current-state OPV63 scenario, based on commercially oriented module cost assumptions and 63 W m −2 output, remains economically constrained across most configurations, although NPVs at low PV coverage indicate that moderate improvements in efficiency or costs could enable feasibility. When crop yield impacts are incorporated, profitability becomes strongly crop-dependent. High-value crops such as strawberries are better able to offset PV investment costs, as the shading effect can enhance crop yields. Lower-value crops remain economically challenging. Sensitivity analysis indicates that, if the PV system alone does not achieve break-even, additional crop revenues of up to 4700€ year −1 in Bari and 6400€ year −1 in Almería are required to reach economic break-even. Conversely, economically viable configurations can withstand revenue losses of up to 3600€ year −1 and 1600€ year −1 , respectively. Overall, the results demonstrate that photovoltaic greenhouse systems can become economically viable under favorable demand conditions, suitable crop selection and future OPV cost and performance improvements.

title: Advances in sorption-based thermochemical energy storage: from material properties to prototype-level performance
Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: Robotic inspection and maintenance for energy infrastructure: a systematic review and future perspectives
From biological principles to battery interfaces: recent progress in bio-inspired design for aqueous zinc-ion batteries
Ultra‐Stable Phosphide Barrier Layer for Thermoelectric Bismuth Telluride
abstract: ABSTRACT The long‐term reliability of bismuth telluride (BT) thermoelectric power generation devices is severely constrained by the lack of reliable barrier layers. In this work, Ni 2 P is proposed as an ultra‐stable barrier layer for N‐type BT (N–BT). The low thermodynamic driving force for interfacial reaction and the sluggish Ni migration in Ni 2 P together ensure the favorable chemical inertness of the Ni 2 P/N–BT interface, while atomic‐scale bonding endows the interface with high bonding energy, leading to the lowest interfacial contact resistivity (∼1 µΩ cm 2 ), highest bonding strength (∼20 MPa), and longest verified stable duration at 523 K (90 days) among reported barrier layer systems. The resulting seven‐pair BT thermoelectric device achieves a maximum energy conversion efficiency of 6.9% at a temperature difference of 230 K. This work not only addresses the long‐standing bottleneck in power generation applications of BT‐based devices since the 1950s, but also provides guidance for barrier layer design in other thermoelectric systems.

title: Materials Control of Nitric Oxide in Cancer Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitric oxide (NO) can suppress antitumor immunity, support tumor adaptation, or promote immune‐mediated killing, making its therapeutic manipulation highly dependent on exposure. This Review examines how materials control NO source, localization, release kinetics, and chemical fate in cancer immunotherapy, with particular attention to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). We analyze polymeric donors, nanocarriers, injectable depots, and strategies for restricting endogenous NO production, linking their physicochemical properties to target exposure and immune function. Evidence from checkpoint‐treated models is distinguished from mechanisms established with other therapies and from human associations. Comparative analyses separate donor capacity from measured NO exposure, carrier accumulation from cellular delivery, and distant‐tumor control from demonstrated immune memory. Four overlapping endogenous contexts, comprising tumor adaptation, myeloid suppression, vascular dysfunction, and inflammatory effector activity, guide intervention design without constituting validated patient categories. We identify testable predictions concerning cellular selectivity, release kinetics, and spatial pharmacodynamic responses. Translation requires measurements that connect material behavior to a defined NO‐dependent process while demonstrating preservation of beneficial endothelial and immune functions. This framework provides a basis for evaluating when localized NO delivery or selective inhibition may support ICB, while recognizing the limits of current preclinical and clinical evidence.

title: Non‐Precious Metal High‐Entropy Oxide Sub‐1 nm Nanowires for Li‐O 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Highly active and structurally robust cathode catalysts are critically required to boost the electrochemical performance of lithium‐oxygen batteries (LOBs). Herein, a generally synthetic method of non‐precious metal high‐entropy oxide‐polyoxometalate sub‐1 nm nanowires (NPMHEO‐POM SNWs) has been successfully developed induced by POM clusters under mild solvothermal conditions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that the dominantly driving forces for the assembly of POMs and multi‐metal oxides are the Coulomb and van der Waals forces, enabling precise theoretical guidance for targeted material synthesis. Benefiting from the 1D ultrafine structure with fully exposed active sites, the precise adjustment of components optimizing the adsorption capability of intermediate (LiO 2 *) and discharge product (Li 2 O 2 ), and the strong interactions of multi‐metal oxides and POMs contributing to the stability, the BiVZrNiCeO x ‐phosphomolybdic acid SNWs‐based LOB achieves a highly specific capacity of 9944 mAh g −1 and stable cycling durability for 312 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , highlighting their great promise as high‐efficiency electrocatalysts for advanced LOBs.

title: Topological Superlattice Stabilized Layered Oxide Cathodes With Sustainable Anionic Redox
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing the oxygen anionic redox (OAR) at high voltage is envisaged as a fascinating approach to promote the energy density of rechargeable batteries. However, the layered transition metal (TM) oxide cathode materials with OAR activity suffer severely from detrimental phase transformations and local structural disorders, leading to electrochemical performance degradation. Herein, we propose a topological superlattice regulation strategy to construct a cathode material with the Li/Mg/Ni‐triple‐center honeycomb superlattice for sodium‐ion batteries. The combined theoretical and in/ex situ investigations demonstrate that the Li/Mg‐centered superlattice topology activates the OAR reaction to boost specific capacity, while the Ni‐centered honeycomb motif prevents the lattice oxygen release by increasing the TM−O covalency. Furthermore, the multi‐topology superlattice configuration suppresses the P−O phase transition and Li/TM interlayer/intralayer migration to reinforce the honeycomb superstructure stability, improving the oxygen redox reversibility. Consequently, the topological superlattice‐stabilized cathode delivers a high capacity of 242 mAh g −1 and exhibits outstanding cycling stability (91.8% capacity retention after 100 cycles). This work provides new insights into the superstructure regulation of state‐of‐the‐art cathode materials for sustainable batteries.

title: Quicklime Slaking‐Mediated Exothermic Reactions in Polidocanol‐Integrated Ablators with Inhibited Heat Diffusion Enable Cancer Thermal Ablation
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite showing a wide application in tumor therapy, the clinically‐used exogenous thermal ablation still suffers from uncontrollable temperature field with rapid heat diffusion. Here an endogenous trigger‐encouraged thermal ablation, namely exothermic reaction‐based thermal ablation (ERTA) based on quicklime slaking and acid‐base neutralization reactions, has been established, wherein CaO nanoparticles were encapsulated with Ag nanoparticles by liposomes to construct ERTA ablators. CaO consumes H 2 O and H + after exothermic reactions to give birth to Ca 2+ and heat. Liposome shell prolongs ERTA via limiting the exothermic reaction rate, and intracellular Ca 2+ overload unites with Ag nanoparticles to produce antitumor ROS to boost cancer ERTA. Importantly, polidocanol‐based foam sclerosing agent (PFSA) with low heat conductivity was integrated to inhibit heat diffusion and confine heat in tumor to elevate temperature and enhance ERTA efficiency. Additionally, PFSA as a routine clinical embolism agent destroys intratumoral blood vessels to occlude blood vessels and establish starvation therapy, which further improves PFSA‐enhanced ERTA efficiency. Consequently, such ERTA‐based ablators and PFSA‐integrated ones outperform the scale‐matched microwave ablation and laboratory‐in photothermal ablation in repressing subcutaneous and orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma, and orthotopic pancreatic cancer. This endogenous trigger‐activated thermal ablation method provides distinctive insights into thermal ablation, presenting a new thermal ablation protocol.

title: Directional Nitrite Spillover Couples to Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Networks for Ampere-Level Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia is often constrained by the proton-coupled hydrogenation of adsorbed nitrite (*NO2), a step commonly accelerated through hydrogen spillover and local reactive-hydrogen (*H) supply. This hydrogen-centered view, however, treats *NO2 largely as a passive intermediate and overlooks whether its migration can reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen-bond-network environment required for downstream hydrogenation. Here, we show that directional *NO2 spillover couples site-specific intermediate transport with interfacial hydrogen-bond-network reorganization. In a Cu–Ag dual-site model interface, nitrate activation and *NO2 formation occur preferentially on the Cu sites, whereas migrated *NO2 species are stabilized and hydrogenated on the Ag-associated sites. In situ spectroscopy, kinetic isotope measurements, distribution-of-relaxation-time analysis, and theoretical simulations reveal that this Cu-to-Ag relay enriches K+-associated interfacial water, reinforces hydrogen-bond connectivity, and facilitates *H delivery for *NO2 hydrogenation. The optimized CuAg N-doped carbon (CuAg–N-C) achieves near-unity Faradaic efficiency (FE) for NH3 with a yield rate of 411.8 mmol g–1 h–1 and retains 83% FE at 1 A cm–2 in a flow cell. The catalyst further retains substantial nitrate-to-ammonia recovery in simulated and authentic industrial water matrices. More broadly, this work establishes *NO2 spillover as a dynamic interfacial mechanism linking intermediate transport, water-network organization, and proton-coupled nitrogen conversion, providing a framework for sustaining molecular-scale selectivity under chemically complex reaction environments.

title: Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution Catalysis with a Europium Photocatalyst for Single Functional Group Cross-Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lanthanide photocatalysis has emerged as a promising alternative to precious-metal systems due to its earth abundance, low toxicity, and unique photophysical properties. However, reported lanthanide-based photocatalysts have primarily focused on the generation of reactive radical species, with limited ability to control product selectivity in bond-forming processes. Here we report a single europium-cryptate catalyst that enables selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling of benzyl chlorides by combining single-electron transfer-driven radical generation with bimolecular homolytic substitution reactivity. The reaction proceeds through a Eu(II)-benzyl intermediate that initiates single-electron transfer to form a benzyl radical, followed by SH2 with a Eu(III)-benzyl species to forge the cross-coupling product. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for designing selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling reactions using lanthanide metals, paving the way for the broader application of lanthanide-based photocatalysts in organic synthesis.

title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) is a widely used film-forming additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes (LMAs), yet its intrinsic interfacial chemistry remains elusive because its reactions are coupled with those of solvents and Li salts in conventional electrolytes. Herein, a solvent-free, dry-processed poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolyte (PEO@Dry) is developed as a platform to isolate the interfacial reactions of FEC without interference from traditional liquid organic solvents. PEO@Dry retains the intrinsic interfacial reactivity of PEO and LiTFSI while eliminating solvent-derived interference. FEC is found to undergo a spontaneous chemical reaction with Li metal before electrochemical reduction, producing a dense LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that is subsequently reinforced by organic species derived from the electrochemical reactions. The resulting SEI exhibits a well-defined composition and robust structure, leading to an enhanced interfacial stability and electrochemical performance. Comparative research with a DME-based liquid electrolyte reveals that FEC (DME@FEC) follows distinct reaction pathways depending on its solvation state. In the solvent-free PEO@Dry system, free FEC undergoes sequential chemical and electrochemical reduction to form an inorganic-rich SEI, whereas in the liquid electrolyte, FEC participates in Li+ solvation and competes with other electrolyte components, yielding a more complex SEI. This work clarifies the interfacial mechanism of FEC and establishes a general solvent-free platform for mechanistic studies of electrolyte additives on LMAs.

title: Sequence-Regulated Adhesion of Poly(diethyl glycolide- alt -β-butyrolactone) Synthesized via Enantiomorphic Site-Assisted Stereospecific Alternating Copolymerization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Biodegradable polyesters can be promising adhesives for their inherent biodegradability, yet their adhesive performance still requires substantial enhancement to meet practical demands. In this work, the alternating sequence effect on adhesive property was explored in the alternating copolymer of S,S-diethylglycolide (S,S-EG, derived from α-hydroxybutyric acid, i.e., α-ethyl-glycolic acid) and R-β-butyrolactone (R-BBL, derived from β-hydroxybutyric acid). However, the alternating copolymerization of these two monomers is still a challenge due to their distinct chemical structures and the inherent competition between cross-propagation and homopropagation. Herein, the successful alternating copolymerization of S,S-EG and R-BBL was reported with an alternating probability of 0.96 through an enantiomorphic site-assisted stereospecific alternating copolymerization strategy using new 1,1′-bi-2-naphthol (BINOL)-derived axially chiral yttrium complex catalysts. Remarkably, the lap-shear adhesion strength of the resulting copolyesters on stainless steel reaches a high level of 10.5 MPa, correlating positively with the increased regularity of the alternating sequence. This improvement can be attributed to the combined effects of interchain electrostatic interactions and viscoelastic behavior, which suggests that monomer sequence can also serve as a molecular parameter for regulating interfacial adhesion performance.

The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

Critical raw material intensity of electricity generation technologies: A probabilistic and multicriteria approach applied to the European Union
abstract: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do not support robust comparisons between electricity generation technologies for decision-making in energy planning and policy. In this context, the present study proposes a probabilistic multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework to assess and rank electricity generation technologies according to their material requirements in t/MWh. It incorporates at least one method from each major MADM family and includes strategies to enhance resilience against rank reversal. Material consumptions are aggregated into satisfaction or criticality indices, while Monte Carlo simulation captures uncertainty and variability in consumption, lifetimes, and operational conditions. The methodology is applied to the EU including eight electricity generation technologies (wind, solar PV, solar CSP, hydro, biomass and waste, nuclear, coal, and natural gas) and 33 raw materials. Despite minor differences among MADM methods, the framework consistently converges on a ranking in which wind and solar PV are the most material-critical technologies, followed by solar CSP; coal, natural gas and nuclear occupy intermediate positions; biomass and waste, and hydro are the least critical alternatives. These findings highlight that EU decarbonisation strategies must be complemented by targeted raw material policies, including diversification of supply, recycling, material substitution, and strategic planning, to ensure that the transition to renewable electricity is not only low-carbon but also materially resilient and secure.

Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
abstract: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.

Regional infrastructure repurposing: Pathways from assessment to geothermal energy production and storage
abstract: Addressing the growing demand for sustainable energy, we explore the innovative potential of repurposing existing subsurface infrastructure for geothermal energy production and energy storage. We present an integrated technical, economic, and legal framework for repurposing regional-scale infrastructure to systematically evaluate and optimize geothermal resource utilization. The states of Berlin and Brandenburg in Germany serve as a model area, with field studies in Groß Schönebeck and Lusatia demonstrating practical infrastructure repurposing. Results show that 12 of the 17 evaluated wells are potentially suitable for repurposing, with hydrothermal energy (HE) emerging as the most promising option. Economic viability is achievable by targeting the Middle Buntsandstein formation at depths exceeding 2400 meters and temperatures above 86 ∘ C, utilizing well doublets with a minimum of 750-meter spacing. Reservoir simulations indicate that optimized development schemes can achieve gross thermal power ranging from 2.9 to 7.6 M W t h with a Levelized Cost of Heat (LCOH) ranging from € 0.035/kWh to € 0.08/kWh. This is achievable through exploration near existing wells and direct connection to district heating networks. While Borehole Heat Exchangers (BHEs) offer faster implementation, their economic viability is challenging due to low thermal power and proximity requirements. Recognizing a mismatch between existing subsurface data and heat demand areas, the Landesamt für Bergbau, Geologie und Rohstoffe (LBGR) has initiated a new 2D seismic exploration campaign in 2025 for the Lower Lusatia area, leveraging well-established district heating and hydrocarbon infrastructure. This research demonstrates an economic strategy for reusing infrastructure for heating and energy storage, supported by strategic government initiatives, and provides a replicable decision-making workflow to guide geothermal energy development.
