However, practical Li‐S batteries require high‐mass‐loading sulfur cathodes and lean‐electrolyte operation, where inefficient sulfur conversion is severely amplified by mechanical instability and high electrode tortuosity. Herein, a phase separation electrode is introduced as an electrode‐level strategy to regulate sulfur redox microenvironment. Controlled solvent‐nonsolvent exchange during phase separation chemically manages polymer demixing, producing an optimized isopropanol‐derived phase separation electrode (PSE‐IPA) with electrolyte‐accessible pores with low tortuosity. Such an architecture facilitates lithium‐ion flux and regulates polysulfide distribution within the cathode, enabling efficient and reversible sulfur conversion. Overpotential deconvolution reveals reduced activation and concentration polarizations during lithium sulfide (Li 2 S) nucleation and growth, while operando impedance and X‐ray diffraction analyses confirm suppressed resistance evolution and reversible sulfur‐Li 2 S phase conversion. Consequently, PSE‐IPA enables an ultrahigh sulfur loading of 13.5 mg cm −2 with an areal capacity of 14.6 mAh cm −2 under a lean electrolyte‐to‐sulfur (E/S) ratio of 5 µL mg −1 . Importantly, a double‐stacked pouch‐type Li‐S battery delivers 298 Wh kg −1 , including package materials under practical conditions with a sulfur loading of 9.6 mg cm −2 and E/S ratio of 3.5 µL mg −1 .

title: Perovskite Bandgap‐Driven SAM Engineering for Hole‐Selective Contacts
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have revolutionized hole‐selective contacts in inverted p‐i‐n perovskite solar cells (PSCs), enabling dopant‐free operation, minimal parasitic absorption, and precise work function tuning. However, the diverse interfacial demands across narrow‐bandgap (NBG, 1.2–1.42 eV), medium‐bandgap (MBG, 1.42–1.65 eV), and wide‐bandgap (WBG, >1.65 eV) perovskites reveal that conventional carbazole‐based SAMs exhibit performance limitations tied to bandgap‐specific challenges. NBG systems suffer from Sn 2 + oxidation and deep valence‐band mismatches requiring enhanced passivation, while MBG compositions (the workhorse of single‐junction PSCs) demand balanced energetics and uniform coverage to minimize hysteresis and enable scalable fabrication, and WBG compositions demand aligned valence band maximum (VBM) levels and suppressed halide segregation for tandem applications. This review studied the bandgap‐dependent requirements for SAMs in perovskite solar cells, systematically correlating perovskite bandgap regimes with the corresponding interfacial and electronic design criteria of SAM molecules. Based on these insights, we propose targeted SAM tailoring strategies optimized for narrow‐, medium‐, and wide‐bandgap perovskites. Furthermore, we outline design principles for integrating such tailored SAMs into multi‐junction perovskite solar cells, providing a prospective pathway toward enhancing device performance and facilitating the commercialization of perovskite‐based photovoltaic technologies.

title: Layered Bi‐Pt3Ni Dilute Nanoalloy Boosting Hydrogen Evolution Electrocatalysis in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering nanoalloys can enable advanced low‐Pt electrocatalysts for alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet a challenge remains in terms of the arrangement of multimetallic active sites to simultaneously achieve high catalytic activity and stability. In this work, a layer‐engineered dilute Pt 74 Ni 23 Bi 3 nanoalloy is developed as a highly active and stable composition toward alkaline HER, which is achieved via forming atomic‐layered PtNiBi shell on intermetallic PtBi nanoplates followed by a facile acid treatment. The hollow Pt 74 Ni 23 Bi 3 shell exhibits an ultralow overpotential of 7.0 mV at ‐10 mA cm −2 in 1.0 M KOH, owing to its faster Volmer‐Tafel mechanism. The assembled anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) achieves a low cell voltage of 1.656 V at 1.0 A cm −2 and remains steady at industrial current density. Density functional theory calculations further reveal a complementary Pt‐Ni functionality that Ni preferentially anchors H 2 O and stabilizes OH*, whereas neighboring Pt sites provide a slightly more favorable pathway for H 2 O dissociation and a weaker H* binding environment favorable for H 2 formation. This work provides a general strategy to engineer sophisticated nanoalloys at atomic‐scale, and advances the development of high‐performance electrocatalysts in particular.

title: Dynamic Spatial Programming of Active–Active Antagonistic Fiber Architectures for Enhanced Morphing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Programming multiple deformation modes within a continuous liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) filament remains challenging because molecular alignment and active‐material distribution are typically coupled to the external printing path. Here, a rotational multimaterial printing strategy is introduced that encodes two co‐curable LCE phases with opposite free thermal strains within individual fibers. These antagonistic free strains act cooperatively after co‐curing to generate internal strain mismatch and structural deformation. A dual‐channel rotating nozzle co‐extrudes a thermally contracting nematic LCE and a thermally elongating smectic LCE, while nozzle angle, angular velocity, and flow‐rate ratio prescribe their cross‐sectional and axial distributions. Discrete and continuous rotation enable contraction, elongation, in‐plane bending, out‐of‐plane curling, and helical coiling without changing the filament centerline. Under matched conditions, the active–active fibers exhibit an approximately 1.6‐fold increase in curvature relative to the active–passive controls, while simultaneous co‐curing increases interfacial peel strength by approximately 30 times that achieved by sequential curing. The same encoding strategy extends from individual fibers to grids and Gaussian‐curvature surfaces and enables force‐generating strips, thermal protection, self‐sensing, particle sorting, and adaptive gripping. Rotational multimaterial printing therefore decouples intra‐filament architecture from toolpath geometry and provides a general route to spatially programmable active fibers.

title: Spin‐State Regulation Engineering of Pyrophosphate‐Based Polyanionic Cathodes for Ultra‐Long‐Life Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing sodium‐ion cathodes that combine high energy density with ultralong cycling stability requires structural regulation beyond conventional surface modification or single‐site doping. Here, a spin‐state regulation strategy is introduced for iron‐based pyrophosphate cathodes by synergistically substituting Mn and F into Na 3.12 Fe 2.44 (P 2 O 7 ) 2 . The resulting Na 2.92 Fe 2.24 Mn 0.2 (P 2 O 6.9 F 0.1 ) 2 (NFMnPF) modulates an intermediate‐spin Fe 2+ configuration that redistributes charge within the Fe─O─P framework and promotes cooperative Fe─O/Mn─O bond evolution during Na + insertion/extraction. Magnetic susceptibility, Mössbauer spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance, UV‐vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, conductivity measurements, in situ x‐ray diffraction, and density functional theory collectively support this electronic structural coupling, revealing narrowed electronic band gap, reduced Na + migration barrier, suppressed volume variation, and highly reversible lattice evolution. As a result, the co‐doped cathode delivers 115.75 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C, an energy density of 336 Wh kg −1 , and exceptional high‐rate durability, retaining 70% capacity after 24 000 cycles at 10 C and 80.93% after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. A hard‐carbon//NFMnPF full cell further achieves energy density of 319.54 Wh kg −1 (based on the cathode active mass) with stable cycling. These findings establish spin‐state mediated cooperative strain accommodation as a powerful design principle for intrinsically durable polyanionic sodium‐ion cathodes.

title: Cyclic Dimer Acceptor towards 20.9% Efficient Organic Solar Cells by Suppressing Electron‐Phonon Coupling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Minimizing non‐radiative recombination energy loss (Δ E nr ) remains a critical challenge in boosting the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a novel cyclic dimer acceptor, CR‐L8, rationally designed via an asymmetric linking strategy. In this molecular architecture, a thiophene linker extends the conjugated plane, while a flexible 1,6‐di(thiophen‐2‐yl)hexane chain acts as the another linker, synergistically modulating molecular conformation, packing, and aggregation. Compared to its linear analogues, the cyclic configuration significantly suppresses molecular vibrations and electron‐phonon coupling, leading to a substantially enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield and effective blockage of non‐radiative recombination channels. Importantly, CR‐L8‐based blend maintains favorable molecular packing and double‐fibril morphology, ensuring efficient charge transport. As a result, the D18:CR‐L8 device achieves a record efficiency of 17.23%, which is the highest value reported to date for OSCs employing cyclic dimer acceptor. Moreover, the Δ E nr of 0.155 eV in D18:CR‐L8 device is the lowest among OSCs with efficiencies exceeding 15%. Finally, incorporating CR‐L8 as the third component into D18:L8‐BO blend further boosts the performance, with the optimized ternary device achieving an impressive efficiency of 20.92%. This work pioneers a cyclic acceptor design strategy that mitigates non‐radiative recombination, offering a new molecular blueprint for high‐performance organic photovoltaics.

title: Colloidally Prepared Homogeneous Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Efficient Tandem Solar Cells with Industrial Silicon
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites, based on mixed halide-cation compositions, are widely employed as top cells in perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells to overcome the theoretical limitations of single-junction devices and exploit the full potential of crystalline silicon photovoltaics. However, uncontrolled nucleation rates and disordered crystallization kinetics in WBG perovskites pose a grave challenge to the preparation of phase-homogeneous perovskite films. Herein, we identify the undesirable precursor suspension as the main underlying reason for the compositional inhomogeneity and propose a colloidal engineering strategy to reconstruct the perovskite intermediate complex. According to classical colloidal theory and theoretical calculations, long-chain alkylphosphonic acid molecules are selected to precisely regulate colloidal structures and properties via their specific coordination strengths, leading to colloid-guided rapid nucleation and slow crystallization processes. Assisted by the uniform colloidal nucleation template, the prepared WBG perovskite films with compositional homogenization and reduced trap density enable tandem devices based on industrial silicon heterojunction cells to yield a champion power conversion efficiency of 34.01% (a certified reverse-scan PCE of 33.65%) for a 1 cm2 active area. The resultant encapsulated tandem device maintains 93% and 88% of its initial efficiency after 1211 h and 1000 h of one-sun operation at 25 and 65 °C, respectively, under their maximum power points.

title: A Phosphonium Relay for Integrated Cleavage‐to‐Cyclization of Cyclic Peptides
abstract: ABSTRACT Head‐to‐tail macrocyclization of peptides is typically performed through stepwise workflows that separate resin cleavage, isolation of linear intermediates, and subsequent cyclization, largely due to incompatible activation requirements for each transformation. Here we report a phosphonium‐mediated relay that unifies these steps within a single activation node. In this design, an electrophile‐activated phosphonium species promotes cleavage from standard 2‐chlorotrityl chloride (2‐CTC) resin and is proposed to enable in situ formation of a C ‐terminally activated intermediate for intramolecular amidation. The strategy directly couples cleavage to cyclization on standard peptide supports without auxiliary linkers, intermediate purification, or high‐dilution cyclization conditions. The method is compatible with diverse peptide sequccnces and functional handles and can be integrated into a closed‐loop automated workflow for end‐to‐end synthesis, with advantages for hydrophobic substrates by avoiding isolation of poorly soluble linear intermediates such as Vespid chemotactic peptide 5f . Process‐level benchmarking against side‐chain anchoring further demonstrated favorable process metrics and gram‐scale scalability. This work establishes a linker‐free cleavage‐to‐cyclization strategy and provides a practical framework for integrated and automation‐compatible cyclic peptide synthesis.

title: Robust Tetrazine‐Bridged Binuclear Iridium(III) Complex Featuring Tunable Conformational Dynamics for Efficient Photothermal Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing near‐infrared photothermal materials with outstanding conversion efficiency and high photostability remains a critical challenge for small‐molecule systems. We report a unique donor‐acceptor platform based on a binuclear iridium(III) architecture featuring a bridging electron‐deficient 1,2,4,5‐tetrazine ligand. The complex exhibits strong and broad absorption up to 1200 nm in solution and 1500 nm in the solid state, significantly outperforming other metal complexes. Temperature‐ and solvent‐dependent 1 H NMR coupled with X‐ray diffraction suggest the ‘butterfly‐like’ conformational behavior of the complex, while theoretical calculations identify low‐energy charge‐transfer transitions from cyclometalated cores to the tetrazine moiety as the origin of the exceptionally high absorbance and efficient non‐radiative relaxation. This facilitates robust photothermal activity across three different excitation wavelengths (635, 808, 980 nm), delivering an excellent conversion efficiency of 94.9% at 808 nm (acetone solvate) along with long‐term stability over multiple cycles (CHCl 3 /CH 2 Cl 2 ‐derived phase), uniquely tunable through crystal packing engineering. When applied to cellulose paper, the complex drives solar‐to‐thermal water evaporation with an efficiency of 86.6%. This high performance is accompanied by exceptional photostability under prolonged irradiation, ranking the developed material among the most competitive systems reported. Overall, this work establishes bridging 1,2,4,5‐tetrazines and crystal engineering as powerful tools for designing high‐performance organometallic photothermal materials.

title: Photo‐Induced Multi‐Physical Field Synergy for Direct Natural Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct natural seawater electrolysis offers a sustainable route for green hydrogen production, yet severe performance degradation stemming from irreversible interfacial precipitation hinders its practical application. Herein, a photo‐induced multi‐physical field synergy strategy is developed to dynamically regulate interfacial OH − transfer and eliminate cathode pH self‐amplifying polarization. A plasmonic photo‐responsive electrode constructed via ultrathin amorphous MoO 3 coating on PtMo alloy nanoparticles is fabricated to integrate photo‐induced asymmetric electric field (PAEF) and localized photothermal field (PLPF). Such a well‐designed core‐shell structure delivers a record‐high industrial current density of 8 A cm −2 at low overpotential (433 mV) in alkaline seawater. In situ characterizations and spectroscopic analyses verify that the dual fields optimize the electric double‐layer ion distribution and drive microscale thermal convection, accelerating OH − dissipation. Benefiting from the above, the engineered light‐responsive catalytic system exhibits a low overpotential of 232 mV at 100 mA cm −2 in natural seawater, alongside anti‐precipitation ability, and maintains stable operation over 100 h (6.2% decay). A photo‐assisted asymmetric electrolyzer achieves a low cell voltage of 2.27 V at 0.5 A cm −2 for seawater splitting, which realizes effective green hydrogen generation under fluctuating natural solar light (normalized ramp‐following ratio > 0.9).

title: One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular design of ferroelectric nematics has primarily focused on optimizing highly polar rigid mesogenic cores, whereas the role of flexible aliphatic segments in regulating molecular conformation and polar ordering remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that exchanging the positions of a methylene group and the ether oxygen within the linkage between a polar rigid core and an aliphatic tail (Ar‐O‐CH 2 ‐ versus Ar‐CH 2 ‐O‐) reshapes the molecular conformational landscape and profoundly influences the stability of the ferroelectric nematic (N F ) phase. Molecules with a stronger preference for bent, pear‐like effective geometries exhibit significantly enhanced N F stability, accompanied by reduced splay and bend elastic constants in the apolar nematic phase, and lower apparent activation barriers for dipolar reorientation. Further elongation of the flexible segment introduces competing packing motifs and gives rise to a domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C (SmC AF ) phase. These findings establish conformational bending as a molecular‐shape parameter for controlling hierarchical ferroelectric and antiferroelectric liquid‐crystalline order, bridging the design principles of conventional bent‐core layered ferroelectrics with emerging rod‐like fluid ferroelectric materials.

title: Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse
abstract: ABSTRACT The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual‐inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony. Herein, we report squaraine‐based photocatalysts as a single‐agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation, IITC depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently, IITC ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy IITC undergoes self‐immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post‐treatment. This self‐eliminating, metabolism‐targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.

title: Revisiting the Role of Dynamic Linkages in Polymer Compatibilization Using Diazirine–Anhydride Conjugates
abstract: ABSTRACT Small‐molecule crosslinkers can compatibilize mixed plastics through reactive extrusion, providing a potential solution to extant challenges in polymer recycling. Existing studies have prioritized the use of crosslinker molecules that incorporate dynamic linkages between reactive warheads; however, the absolute requirement for these dynamic groups remains unproven, and previous comparisons of static versus dynamic crosslinkers employed molecules with vastly different C–H insertion efficiencies. In this study, we employed chemistry‐explicit reaction molecular dynamics simulations, small‐molecule surrogates of interface reactions, phase morphology studies, and mechanical analysis to explicitly test hypotheses around the value of dynamic linkages. Using rationally designed, reactivity‐matched pairs of dynamic and static crosslinkers, we found the presence of dynamic anhydride linkages did not generally improve compatibilization efficacy. Instead, dynamic exchange enabled reorganization of compatibilizing hetero‐crosslinks into non‐compatibilizing homo‐crosslinks over time, while facilitating other undesirable reactivity pathways. Our findings indicate compatibilization performance is dictated by physicochemical control over crosslinker distribution, rather than dynamic bonding, and that the kinetics of dynamic exchange must be tightly regulated to avoid undermining compatibilization. We anticipate that these findings will guide the development of improved crosslinker reagents for polymer compatibilization and other materials applications.

title: Anionic Lone‐Pair‐Like Electrons Induced Ultra‐Low Lattice Thermal Conductivity and High Thermoelectric Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT The traditional lone‐pair electron strategy primarily reduces lattice thermal conductivity ( κ L ) by enhancing anharmonic lattice vibrations. However, this mechanism has long been considered to exist only in specific cations with ns 2 electron configurations (e.g. Sb 3+ , Bi 3+ ), severely restricting the broader applicability of this lone‐pair‐based approach. In this study, CuInSnSe 4 is successfully synthesized via atomic cross‐substitution from the diamondoid CuInSe 2 , wherein the Se atoms exhibit an anionic lone‐pair‐like electronic behavior, revealing a new approach to reducing κ L that differs from conventional cation‐based mechanisms. In contrast to the traditional mechanism that relies on cations to enhance lattice anharmonicity, the anionic lone‐pair electrons weaken the Se‐Se interactions, flatten the optical phonon branches, and consequently significantly expand the scattering phase space, providing more scattering channels for phonons. This anionic lone‐pair electron strategy reduces the room‐temperature κ L from 4.48 to 1.26 W m −1 K −1 . Ultimately, the predicted optimal thermoelectric figure of merit ( ZT ) for p‐type and n‐type CuInSnSe 4 attains values of 1.99 and 0.79, respectively. This work systematically expands the conventional application boundaries of the lone‐pair electron strategy and elucidates a fundamentally distinct mechanism for κ L reduction, providing a new theoretical basis for designing and developing novel high‐efficiency thermoelectric materials with intrinsically low κ L .

title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the electron‐transfer pathways and the mechanism in facilitating polysulfide conversion is crucial for the rational design of catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries. Herein, we designed an NbSe 2 model catalyst to investigate the electron‐transfer pathways at sublayer transition metal cation sites through coordination field modulation, and revealed the relationship between electron transfer and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, the σ *– σ and π *– σ electron transfer channels at transition metal sites are identified in terms of the coordination field theory and hybrid orbital theory, where the σ *– σ channel exhibits higher electron transfer efficiency and therefore enhances the adsorption and conversion role of transition metal sites in polysulfides. The designed trigonal prismatic NbSe 2 exhibits a reversible capacity up to 799 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 5 C, and the battery maintains stability under ultra‐high sulfur loading, achieving a capacity retention rate as high as 95.85%. From an electronic perspective, this work reveals the role of coordination fields on catalytic activity, providing new insights for the rational design of catalysts in metal–S batteries.

title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF 3 ) removal from monofluoromethane (CH 3 F) exemplifies this problem: CH 3 F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF 3 is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF 3 from CH 3 F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF 6 2– pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF 3 while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH 3 F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH 3 F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF 3 under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm 3 /g of CHF 3 at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF 3 produced CH 3 F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF 3 at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.

title: An In Situ Amorphous Thermoconversion Strategy for Macroscopic Glass Heterojunctions
abstract: ABSTRACT Heterojunction fabrication has long been constrained by the stringent lattice‐matching requirements between dissimilar components, limiting the accessible material combinations and processing routes. Here, we report an amorphous thermoconversion strategy for constructing hybrid glass heterojunctions in situ. In this approach, structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystal structures generates divergent luminescence across amorphous phases, giving rise to a new family of halide glass heterojunctions. These hybrid halide glasses display excitation‐dependent and time‐gated persistent luminescence that is color‐tunable across a 160 nm wavelength window, a property that enables direct optical visualization and confers broad photonic versatility. Beyond their optical attributes, the resulting macroscopic glass heterojunctions exhibit well‐defined mechanical rigidity and arbitrary processability, supporting spatially resolved fluorescence and persistent luminescence outputs alongside one‐dimensional (1D) optical waveguiding at losses that surpass those of state‐of‐the‐art crystalline counterparts. Therefore, this work delivers the demonstration of macroscopic heterojunctions in halide supramolecular glasses and establishes a scalable route to multi‐channel, low‐dimensional optical waveguide for information storage and encryption applications.

title: Field‐Free Brightening of Dark Excitons in a Two‐Dimensional Perovskite by Organic Spacer Fluorination
abstract: ABSTRACT Modifying the organic spacer is a powerful way to tune the excitonic properties of two‐dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (R–P) hybrid halide perovskites. Here, fluorination of the spacer, replacing phenylethylammonium (PEA) with 4‐fluorophenylethylammonium (4‐FPEA), is shown to brighten dark excitons in (4‐FPEA) 2 PbI 4 without an external magnetic field. Below 30 K, (4‐FPEA) 2 PbI 4 exhibits a sharp photoluminescence (PL) signal 7.8 meV below the bright exciton that is absent in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 . Its long lifetime, strong linear polarization, and quadratic magnetic‐field dependence identify this signal as dark‐exciton emission. A magnetic field of up to 0.7 T changes this emission only weakly, whereas it strongly brightens dark excitons in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 . The response is also asymmetric, with its minimum displaced from the zero field. This offset, absent in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 , points to a built‐in mixing of dark and bright states that acts as an internal field. Under two‐photon excitation, which generates excitons deep inside the crystal, the dark‐exciton emission persists. The brightening, therefore, originates in the bulk, unlike the surface‐related brightening reported for other 2D R–P perovskites. These results identify spacer fluorination as a simple chemical route to access spin‐forbidden excitonic states in 2D R–P perovskites.

title: Thermodynamically Controlled Multiphase Evolution in Single‐Crystal Cation‐Disordered Li‐Ion Cathode Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Mn‐based disordered rock‐salt (Mn‐DRX) cathodes are promising materials for Li‐ion batteries, yet their application is limited by sluggish Li transport, voltage instability, and capacity fading. Here, we show that thermodynamic control of multiphase evolution from single‐crystal Mn‐DRX overcomes these limitations. Using grand‐potential phase diagrams with in situ and ex situ X‐ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy, we demonstrate that DRX composition and annealing conditions govern transformation into nanocomposites containing DRX, spinel, and monoclinic layered phases, with anatase formation predicted in specific Li–Mn–Ti–O compositions. Oxidative annealing at 300–500°C induces decomposition pathways: Li‐deficient compositions form DRX–spinel (DS) nanocomposites, whereas Li‐rich compositions form DRX–spinel–monoclinic layered (DSM) architectures. Unlike DS materials, which exhibit lower first‐charge capacities than discharge capacities, the monoclinic phase in DSM nanocomposites enables substantially improved first‐charge Li extraction, critical for practical Li‐ion batteries. The DSM nanocomposites deliver reversible capacities approaching 300 mAh g −1 and discharge specific energies exceeding 800 Wh kg −1 , while their cycling stability can be substantially improved by using a highly concentrated electrolyte and restricting the voltage window. This work establishes thermodynamically guided multiphase engineering as a strategy for addressing transport and stability limitations in DRX cathodes.

title: Self‐Sustaining Lattice‐Oxygen Cycling Enables Durable Industrial‐Level Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Lattice oxygen‐mediated seawater oxidation offers fast kinetics for energy‐efficient hydrogen production, but its practical application is hampered by catalyst degradation arising from transient oxygen vacancies and chloride corrosion at industrial current densities. Here we report an Ag‐decorated amorphous RuFeCo layered double hydroxide (Ag‐RuFeCo LDH) that enables self‐sustaining lattice‐oxygen cycling by integrating disorder‐activated lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) with an anion‐selective interface. Ru incorporation induces structural disorder and enhances Fe─O covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen participation in seawater oxidation. Meanwhile, oxophilic silver oxide reconstructed in situ establishes an OH − ‐enriched interfacial environment that mitigates Cl − adsorption and rapidly replenishes LOM‐generated oxygen vacancies, thereby stabilizing the catalyst structure. Consequently, Ag‐RuFeCo LDH requires only 308 mV overpotential to achieve 1.0 A cm −2 in alkaline natural seawater and maintains stable performance during a cumulative operation exceeding 9500 h. An anion‐exchange‐membrane electrolyzer using Ag‐RuFeCo LDH as both electrodes reaches 1.0 A cm −2 at 1.92 V and operates continuously for 1000 h with a low energy consumption of 4.59 kWh Nm −3 H 2 . This strategy successfully overcomes the corrosion bottleneck of LOM in seawater electrolysis and offers a general strategy for durable and sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Multiscale Characterizations Toward Energy Storage Carbon Materials From Precursors to Electrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The sp 2 ‐hybridized carbon materials such as graphite, soft carbon, and hard carbon, are broadly used as anodes for alkali‐metal‐ion batteries owing to their stable and controllable microstructures. However, the inherent structural complexity and multi‐stage synthesis processes of carbon materials pose challenges to their comprehensive characterization, limiting a deeper structural understanding and performance improvement of carbon electrodes. This review establishes a comprehensive characterization framework for the multiscale understanding of carbon materials from their precursors to carbon electrodes. Because the structural features of carbon materials are largely inherited from their precursors, we first summarize the recent advances in the characterization of their molecular structures and pyrolysis behaviors. We then discuss advanced characterization techniques and corresponding analysis methods used to understand the multiscale structures of carbon materials, including particles, microcrystals, and pore structures. We further provide a comprehensive overview of static and real time characterization techniques for studying interfacial ion transport and bulk ion diffusion kinetics in carbon electrodes. On this basis, we draw a decision‐making framework for multiscale characterization to help readers quickly navigate from problem definition to characterization strategy. Finally, we provide future perspectives to facilitate the efficient scientific investigation and rational design of high‐performance carbon materials for alkali‐metal‐ion batteries.

title: Remarkable Low‐Temperature Magnetocaloric Performance in a Frustrated Divalent Eu(II) Magnet Eu 5 FP 3 O 12
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of 3 He‐free sub‐Kelvin adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR), which relies on the magnetocaloric (MC) effect in magnets, is constrained by the lack of magnetic refrigerants operating from several Kelvin to the milli‐Kelvin range. This work reports a geometrically frustrated divalent Eu(II)‐dominated magnet, Eu 5 FP 3 O 12 , designed by combining moderate magnetic frustration with a dense Eu(II) magnetic lattice, which is distinct from conventional trivalent Gd(III)‐based systems. Eu 5 FP 3 O 12 crystallizes in a hexagonal structure in which a subset of magnetic Eu(II) ions occupies a triangular lattice, giving rise to moderate magnetic frustration and a very low magnetic ordering temperature of 530 mK. Consequently, the Eu 5 FP 3 O 12 exhibits a large low‐temperature MC effect with a maximum magnetic entropy change of 64.5 (370.3) J/kg K (mJ/cm 3 K) and a maximum adiabatic temperature change of 16.9 K under a magnetic field variation of 0–5 T. These values substantially surpass the commercial standard Gd 3 Ga 5 O 12 and are comparable to or exceed those of the best reported low‐temperature magnetic refrigerants under comparable conditions. Together with its good environmental stability and facile solid‐state synthesis, these results identify Eu 5 FP 3 O 12 as a promising refrigerant for 3 He‐free ADR applications and highlight the frustrated divalent Eu(II) magnets as a viable design route for low‐temperature magnetic refrigerants.
